title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ
titleEn: Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, ends: Reunion and Ḥasan al-Baṣrī at Court; the Tailor and the Hunchback begins
part: Night 24 · The Tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn ends / The Hunchback's Tale begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 189–199 (Night 24, continuing directly from nights-23), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 24 brings the tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn to its end. The vizier's household discovers that the cook of Damascus is Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan; Shams al-Dīn has him brought to Cairo in a chest, stages the wedding chamber again so that he wakes believing he dreamed it all, and reveals himself as his uncle. The son, the mother and the father are reunited, and Ḥasan al-Baṣrī is presented at the Sultan's court, where his verses and learning make him a boon companion. Harun al-Rashid, hearing it from Jaʿfar, orders it written in gold, and Shahrazād begins the tale of the Tailor, the Hunchback, the Jew and the Christian, which ends the night with the hunchback's death. Verse is copied as printed, and pointed by us only where the print has no marks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-ʿishrūna
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-fourth and-the-twenty,
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-fourth night,
sentences.n: The number is printed nominative, والعشرون, agreeing with اللَّيْلَة, the subject of كانت; that is the ordinary formula and not a Middle Arabic form. I point what is printed.

sentences.t: قَٰلَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ جَدَّةَ عَجِيبٍ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ اغْتَاظَتْ وَنَظَرَتْ لِلْخَادِمِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna jaddata ʿajībin lammā samiʿat kalāmahu ightāẓat wa-naẓarat li-al-khādimi wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O king the-fortunate, that the-grandmother-of ʿAjīb, when she-heard his-speech, was-enraged, and-looked at-the-servant, and-said to-him:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when ʿAjīb's grandmother heard what he said, she flew into a rage, looked at the servant, and said to him,
sentences.n: قلت is printed for قالت; it is read qālat, "she said" (Shahrazād), and is pointed with the dagger alif. The slip recurs in this night. ʿAjīb is the boy, Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan's son. نظرت لِـ, "looked at", is colloquial for Classical نظرت إلى.

sentences.t: وَيْلَكَ أَنْتَ أَفْسَدْتَ وَلَدِي لِأَنَّكَ دَخَلْتَ بِهِ إِلَى دَكَاكِينِ الطَّبَّاخِينَ
sentences.tr: waylaka anta afsadta waladī li-annaka dakhalta bihi ilā dakākīni al-ṭabbākhīna
sentences.l: Woe-to-you! You, you-spoiled my-son, because-you entered with-him to the-shops-of the-cooks.
sentences.i: Woe to you! You have ruined my son, because you took him into the cooks' shops.
sentences.n: وَيْلَكَ, "woe to you!", is a stock scolding, closer to "you wretch!" than to a curse. دخل بِهِ means "went in with him", that is, "took him in".

sentences.t: فَخَافَ الطَّوَاشِي وَأَنْكَرَ وَقَالَ مَا دَخَلْنَا الدُّكَّانَ وَلَكِنْ جُزْنَا جَوَازًا
sentences.tr: fa-khāfa al-ṭawāshī wa-ankara wa-qāla mā dakhalnā al-dukkāna wa-lakin juznā jawāzan
sentences.l: So-feared the-eunuch and-denied, and-said: We-did-not enter the-shop, but we-passed (by) a-passing.
sentences.i: The eunuch was afraid and denied it. He said, "We did not go into the shop; we only passed by."
sentences.n: الطواشي (ṭawāshī) is the Egyptian word for a eunuch servant, here the boy's guardian. جَوَازًا is an absolute object ("we passed a passing"), the Arabic way of saying "we merely passed by".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ وَاللَّهِ إِلَّا دَخَلْنَا وَأَكَلْنَا وَهُوَا حَسَنٌ مِنْ طَعَامِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿajībun wa-Allāhi illā dakhalnā wa-akalnā wa-huwa aḥsanu min ṭaʿāmika
sentences.l: And-said ʿAjīb: By-God, rather we-entered and-we-ate, and-it better than your-food.
sentences.i: But ʿAjīb said, "By God, we did go in, and we ate, and it is better than your food!"
sentences.n: والله إلا دخلنا is an oath with إِلَّا as "on the contrary": "by God, we did go in". The print runs وهو and the alif of أحسن together as وهوا, then writes حسن; it is read wa-huwa aḥsanu, "and it is better", and I point the second word as the comparative (no tanwīn) to match.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ جَدَّتُهُ وَأَخْبَرَتْ أَخُوزَوْجِهَا وَأَغْرَتْهُ عَلَى الْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat jaddatuhu wa-akhbarat akhuwazawjihā wa-aghrathu ʿalā al-khādimi
sentences.l: So-rose his-grandmother, and-told her-husband's-brother, and-incited-him against the-servant.
sentences.i: His grandmother got up and told her brother-in-law, and set him against the servant.
sentences.n: أخوزوجها is the print's single word for أخو زوجها, "her husband's brother": the vizier. I point it as printed, without a space. أغرى عَلَى is "to egg on against".

sentences.t: فَحَضَرَ الْخَادِمُ قُدَّامَ الْوَزِيرِ فَقَالَ لَهُ لِمَ دَخَلْتَ بِوَلَدِي دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ فَخَافَ الْخَادِمُ وَقَالَ مَا دَخَلْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaḍara al-khādimu quddāma al-wazīri fa-qāla lahu li-ma dakhalta bi-waladī dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi fa-khāfa al-khādimu wa-qāla mā dakhalnā
sentences.l: So-attended the-servant in-front-of the-vizier, and-he-said to-him: For-what did-you-enter with-my-son (the) shop-of the-cook? And-feared the-servant and-said: We-did-not enter.
sentences.i: The servant came before the vizier, and he said to him, "Why did you take my son into the cook's shop?" The servant was afraid and said, "We did not go in."
sentences.n: قُدَّامَ, "in front of", is the everyday word for "before". لِمَ is لِـ + مَا, "for what?", that is, "why?", with the alif of مَا dropped.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ دَخَلْنَا وَأَكَلْنَا مِنْ حَبِّ الرُّمَّانِ حَتَّى شَبِعْنَا وَأَسْقَانَا الطَّبَّاخُ أَقْسَمَا بِثَلْجٍ وَسُكَّرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿajībun dakhalnā wa-akalnā min ḥabbi al-rummāni ḥattā shabiʿnā wa-asqānā al-ṭabbākhu aqsamā bi-thaljin wa-sukkarin
sentences.l: And-said ʿAjīb: We-entered and-we-ate from the-grains-of the-pomegranate until we-were-full, and-gave-us-to-drink the-cook aqsamā with-ice and-sugar.
sentences.i: But ʿAjīb said, "We went in and ate pomegranate seeds until we were full, and the cook gave us something to drink, with ice and sugar."
sentences.n: حَبّ الرُّمَّان, literally "grains of the pomegranate", is the dish of pomegranate seeds the boy has been eating. اقسما is obscure and may be corrupt: I point it as printed, أَقْسَمَا ("they two swore"), which makes no sense here. The sense needed is a drink, a sherbet, "with ice and sugar", so perhaps a word for a measure or a portion has been garbled; the translation gives only the sense. أَسْقَانَا is form IV, "gave us to drink".

sentences.t: فَازْدَادَ غَضَبُ الْوَزِيرِ عَلَى الْخَادِمِ وَ سَأَلَهُ فَأَنْكَرَ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ إِنْ كَانَ كَلَامُكَ صَحِيحًا فَانْعَدْ وَكُلْ قُدَّ امَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-izdāda ghaḍabu al-wazīri ʿalā al-khādimi wa saʾalahu fa-ankara fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru in kāna kalāmuka ṣaḥīḥan fa-inʿad wa-kul qudd amanā
sentences.l: So-increased the-anger-of the-vizier against the-servant, and he-asked-him, and-he-denied; and-said to-him the-vizier: If was your-speech true, then sit and-eat before-us.
sentences.i: The vizier's anger at the servant grew, and he questioned him, and the servant denied it again. So the vizier said to him, "If what you say is true, then sit and eat in front of us."
sentences.n: The print has a stray و alone at the line end (و ساله); it is kept apart from the next word. فانعد is almost certainly a misprint for فاقعد, "sit" (ن for ق); I point what is printed, فَانْعَدْ, and read it as "sit". قد امنا is the print's division of قدامنا, "in front of us" (quddāmanā): it is split into قُدَّ and امَنَا, which together read quddāmanā. The same split recurs below.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَدَمَ الْخَادِمُ وَأَرَادَانْ يَأْكُلَ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ وَرَمَى اللُّقْمَةَ وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنِّي شَبْعَانُ مِنَ الْبَارِحَةِ فَعَرَفَ الْوَزِيرُ أَنَّهُ أَكَلَ عِنْدَ الطَّبَّاخِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qadama al-khādimu wa-arādān yaʾkula fa-lam yaqdir wa-ramā al-luqmata wa-qāla yā sayyidī innī shabʿānu mina al-bāriḥati fa-ʿarafa al-wazīru annahu akala ʿinda al-ṭabbākhi
sentences.l: And-at that went-forward the-servant, and-wanted that he-eat, and-not he-was-able; and-he-threw-down the-morsel and-said: O my-lord, I (am) full since the-last-night. And-knew the-vizier that-he ate at the-cook.
sentences.i: At that the servant stepped forward and tried to eat, but he could not. He threw down the morsel and said, "My lord, I have been full since last night." And the vizier knew that he had eaten at the cook's.
sentences.n: وارادان is the print's single word for وأراد أن, "and he wanted to"; I point it as أَرَادَ + أَنْ run together. مِنَ الْبَارِحَةِ, "since last night", uses مِنْ for "since".

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الْعَبِيدَانْ يَطْرَحُوهُ فَطَرَحُوهُ وَنَزَلَ عَلَيْهِ بِالضَّرْبِ الْوَجِيعِ فَاسْتَغَاثَ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-ʿabīdan yaṭraḥūhu fa-ṭaraḥūhu wa-nazala ʿalayhi bi-al-ḍarbi al-wajīʿi fa-istaghātha
sentences.l: So-he-commanded the-slaves that they-throw-him-down, and-they-threw-him-down; and-he-came-down upon-him with-the-beating the-painful, and-he-cried-for-help.
sentences.i: He ordered the slaves to throw him down, and they threw him down, and the vizier came down on him with a painful beating, and the servant cried out for help.
sentences.n: العبيدان is العبيد أن run together, "the slaves, that". After أَنْ the verb يطرحوه is pointed without a final nūn, as the subjunctive requires. نزل عليه بِـ is "fell upon him with", the idiom for laying into someone.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي لَا تَضْرِبْنِي وَأَنَا أَقُولُ لَكَ الصَّحِيحَ فَتَبَطَّلَ عَنْهُ الضَّرْبُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā sayyidī lā taḍribnī wa-anā aqūlu laka al-ṣaḥīḥa fa-tabaṭṭala ʿanhu al-ḍarbu
sentences.l: And-he-said: O my-lord, do-not strike-me, and-I I-tell you the-true. So-ceased from-him the-beating.
sentences.i: He said, "My lord, do not beat me, and I will tell you the truth." And the beating stopped.
sentences.n: وأنا أقول لك is "and I will tell you": the pronoun plus a bare imperfect is a colloquial way of promising. تبطل, "stopped, let up", is colloquial (Classical بَطَلَ); its subject is the beating itself.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ انْطِقْ بِالْحَقِّ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu inṭiq bi-al-ḥaqqi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: Speak with-the-truth.
sentences.i: And he said to him, "Speak the truth."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّا دَخَلْنَا دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ وَهُوَ يَطْبُخُ حَبَّ الرُّمَّانِ فَحَطَّ لَنَا مِنْهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَكَلْتُ عُمْرِي مِثْلَهُ وَلَا ذُقْتُ أَوْحَشَ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي قُدَّ امَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu iʿlam annā dakhalnā dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi wa-huwa yaṭbukhu ḥabba al-rummāni fa-ḥaṭṭa lanā minhu wa-Allāhi mā akaltu ʿumrī mithlahu wa-lā dhuqtu awḥasha min hādhā alladhī qudd amanā
sentences.l: So-he-said to-him: Know that-we entered the-shop-of the-cook, and-he cooking the-grains-of the-pomegranate; and-he-put for-us from-it. By-God, I-have-not eaten my-life (the) like-of-it, and-not I-have-tasted (anything) more-wretched than this which before-us.
sentences.i: He said to him, "Know that we went into the cook's shop while he was cooking pomegranate seeds, and he served us some of it. By God, I have never eaten the like of it in my life, and I have never tasted anything worse than this that is in front of us."
sentences.n: أوحش, literally "more desolate", is used as "worse, more wretched": the servant is comparing the vizier's dish to the cook's. ما أكلت عمري مثله, "I have not eaten my life the like of it", means "never in my life"; عمري is an accusative of time. حَطَّ لَنَا is colloquial for "served us, put out for us". قد امنا is again the split spelling of قدامنا.

sentences.t: فَغَضِبَتْ أُمُّ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَقَالَتْ لَابُدَّانْ تَرُوحَ لِهَذَا الطَّبَّاخِ وَتَجِيبْلَنَا زُبْدِيَّةَ حَبِّ رُمَّانٍ مِنَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ وَتُرِيَهُ لِسَيِّدِكَ حَتَّى يَقُولَ أَيُّهُمَا أَحْسَنُ وَأَطْيَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-ghaḍibat ummu badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-qālat lā budda an tarūḥa li-hādhā al-ṭabbākhi wa-tajībla-nā zubdiyyata ḥabbi rummānin mina alladhī ʿindahu wa-turiyahu li-sayyidika ḥattā yaqūla ayyuhumā aḥsanu wa-aṭyabu
sentences.l: So-became-angry the-mother-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-said: It-must-be that you-go to this the-cook, and-bring-for-us a-bowl-of grains-of pomegranate from that-which (is) with-him, and-show-it to-your-master, until he-says which-of-the-two (is) better and-tastier.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan's mother grew angry and said, "You must go to this cook and bring us a bowl of pomegranate seeds from what he has, and show it to your master, so that he can say which of the two is better and tastier."
sentences.n: The print runs بدر الدين together, and I point it as one word. لابدان is لا بدّ أن, "it must be that"; the verb تروح is colloquial for "go". وتجيبلنا is colloquial, تجيب لنا, "and bring (for) us", with the preposition لِـ run into the verb. أيهما احسن واطيب, "which of the two is better and tastier", has the comparative without a following "than".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَادِمُ نَعَمْ فَفِى الْحَالِ أَعْطَتْهُ زُبْدِيَّةً وَنِصْفَ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khādimu naʿam fa-fī al-ḥāli aʿṭathu zubdiyyatan wa-niṣfa dīnārin
sentences.l: And-said the-servant: Yes. And-at-once she-gave-him a-bowl and-half-a-dinar.
sentences.i: The servant said, "Yes." At once she gave him a bowl and half a dinar.
sentences.n: ففى is printed with ى for ي, and I keep it. فِي الْحَالِ, "at once", is the standard idiom, literally "in the instant".

sentences.t: فَمَضَى الْخَادِمُ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الدُّكَّانِ وَقَالَ لِلطَّبَّاخِ نَحْنُ تَرَاهَنَّا عَلَى طَعَامِكَ فِي بَيْتِ سَيِّدِنَا لِأَنَّ عِنْدَهُمْ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ فَهَاتِ لَنَا بِهَذَا النِّصْفِ دِينَارٍ وَاجْعَلْ بَالَكَ فَقَدْ أَكَلْنَا الضَّرْبَ الْمُوجِعَ عَلَى طَبِيخِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā al-khādimu ḥattā waṣala ilā al-dukkāni wa-qāla li-al-ṭabbākhi naḥnu tarāhannā ʿalā ṭaʿāmika fī bayti sayyidinā li-anna ʿindahum ḥabba rummānin fa-hāti lanā bi-hādhā al-niṣfi dīnārin wa-ijʿal bālaka fa-qad akalnā al-ḍarba al-mūjiʿa ʿalā ṭabīkhika
sentences.l: So-went the-servant until he-reached to the-shop, and-said to-the-cook: We, we-wagered over your-food in the-house-of our-master, because with-them (is) grains-of pomegranate. So bring for-us with this the-half dinar, and-make your-mind; for-indeed we-ate the-beating the-painful over your-cooking.
sentences.i: The servant went on until he reached the shop, and he said to the cook, "We have laid a wager over your food in our master's house, because they have a dish of pomegranate seeds there. So bring us some for this half dinar, and mind what you do, for we have taken a painful beating on account of your cooking."
sentences.n: تراهنا is from تراهن, "to bet with one another". هات, "bring!", is the everyday imperative of "give", and takes بِـ here for the price: "bring for us with this half dinar". اجعل بالك, literally "make your mind", is the colloquial "pay attention, be careful". أكلنا الضرب, "we ate the beating", is a common idiom for "took a beating". هذا النصف دينار has the article on the first term only, as in colloquial usage.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ هَذَا الطَّعَامُ مَا يُحْسِنُهُ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا أَنَا وَوَالِدَتِي وَهِى الْآنَ فِي بِلَادٍ بَعِيدَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-qāla wa-Allāhi hādhā al-ṭaʿāmu mā yuḥsinuhu aḥadun illā anā wa-wālidatī wa-hiya al-āna fī bilādin baʿīdatin
sentences.l: So-laughed Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and-said: By-God, this the-food, not does-it-well anyone except I and-my-mother, and-she now in lands far.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan laughed and said, "By God, nobody can make this dish but I and my mother, and she is now in far-off lands."
sentences.n: بدرالدين is printed as one word and pointed so. ما يحسنه أحد إلا أنا is "nobody does it well (can make it) except me". الآن is printed with the precomposed آ and kept. The cook himself is Ḥasan, the lost son, though nobody in the scene knows it yet.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ غَرَفَ الزُّبْدِيَّةَ وَأَخَذَهَا وَخَتَمَهَا بِالْمِسْكِ وَالْمَاوَرْدِ فَأَخَذَ الْخَادِمُ وَأَسْرَعَ بِهَا حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu gharafa al-zubdiyyata wa-akhadhahā wa-khatamahā bi-al-miski wa-al-māwardi fa-akhadha al-khādimu wa-asraʿa bihā ḥattā waṣala ilayhim
sentences.l: Then-indeed-he ladled the-bowl and-took-it and-sealed-it with-the-musk and-the-rose-water; and-took the-servant and-hurried with-it until he-reached to-them.
sentences.i: Then he ladled out the bowl, took it up, and sealed it with musk and rose water. The servant took it and hurried off with it until he reached them.
sentences.n: ختمها بالمسك والماورد, "sealed it with musk and rose water", is a cook's finishing flourish, not a literal seal. فأخذ الخادم, "the servant took", has no object in the print; the bowl is understood. بِـ after أَسْرَعَ means "hurried with it".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْهَا وَالِدَةُ حَسَنٍ وَذَاقَتْهَا وَنَظَرَتْ حُسْنَ طَعْمِهَا وَجَوْدَةَ طَبْخِهَا فَعَرَفَتْ طَبَّاخَهَا فَصَرَخَتْ ثُمَّ وَقَعَتْ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا فَبُهِتَ الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhathā wālidatu ḥasanin wa-dhāqathā wa-naẓarat ḥusna ṭaʿmihā wa-jawdata ṭabkhihā fa-ʿarafat ṭabbākhahā fa-ṣarakhat thumma waqaʿat maghshiyyan ʿalayhā fa-buhita al-wazīru
sentences.l: So-took-it the-mother-of Ḥasan, and-tasted-it, and-looked-at the-goodness-of its-taste and-the-excellence-of its-cooking; and-she-knew its-cook, and-cried-out; then fell fainted upon-her; and-was-astonished the-vizier.
sentences.i: Ḥasan's mother took it and tasted it, and she noticed how good it tasted and how well it was cooked. She knew who had cooked it, and she cried out and fell to the ground in a faint, and the vizier was struck dumb.
sentences.n: حسن occurs twice: in والدة حسن it is her son's name; in حسن طعمها it is the common noun حُسْن, "goodness", so I point it with a damma. نظرت حسن طعمها is literally "she looked at the goodness of its taste", that is, she took note of it. مغشيا عليها, "covered over on her", is the idiom for fainting; the print has the accusative مغشيا as a circumstantial. بُهِتَ is a passive, "was dumbfounded".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رُشَّ عَلَيْهَا الْمَاوَرْدُ وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ أَفَاقَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma rushsha ʿalayhā al-māwardu wa-baʿda sāʿatin afāqat
sentences.l: Then was-sprinkled upon-her the-rose-water, and-after an-hour she-recovered.
sentences.i: Then rose water was sprinkled over her, and after an hour she came to.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ إِنْكَانَ وَلَدِي فِى الدُّنْيَا فَمَا طَبَخَ هَذَا حَبَّ الرُّمَّانِ إِلَّا هُوَ وَهُوَ وَلَدِي بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ لَاشَكَّ فِيهِ وَلَا مَحَالَةَ لِأَنَّ هَذَا طَعَامٌ وَمَا أَحَدٌ يَطْبُخُهُ غَيْرَهُ إِلَّا أَنَا لِأَنِّي عَلَّمْتُهُ طَبِيخَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat inkāna waladī fī al-dunyā fa-mā ṭabakha hādhā ḥabba al-rummāni illā huwa wa-huwa waladī badru al-dīni ḥasanun lā shakka fīhi wa-lā maḥālata li-anna hādhā ṭaʿāmun wa-mā aḥadun yaṭbukhuhu ghayrahu illā anā li-annī ʿallamtuhu ṭabīkhahu
sentences.l: And-she-said: If-was my-son in the-world, then-not cooked this the-grains-of the-pomegranate but he; and-he (is) my-son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, no doubt in-him and-no avoiding, because this (is) a-dish, and-not anyone cooks-it other-than-him except I, because-I taught-him his-cooking.
sentences.i: She said, "If my son is alive in the world, then nobody cooked this dish of pomegranate seeds but he. And he is my son, Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, beyond all doubt and without fail, because this is a dish that nobody cooks but he and I, for I taught him how to cook it."
sentences.n: إنكان is إن كان run together, "if it be that"; فِي الدُّنْيَا, "in the world", means "alive". لاشك فيه ولا محالة is the stock "without doubt and without fail". The print has no connecting word between ما أحد يطبخه غيره and إلا أنا; it reads "nobody cooks it other than him, except me". طعام here means "a dish": her point is that this is her own recipe, which she taught her son.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَهَا فَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَقَٰلَ وَاشَوْقَاهُ عَلَى رُؤْبَةِ ابْنِ أَخِي أَتُرَيٰ تَجْمَعُ الْأَيَّامُ شَمْلَنَابِهِ وَمَا نَطْلُبُ الِاجْتِمَاعَ بِهِ إِلَّا مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāmahā fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan wa-qāla wā-shawqāhu ʿalā ruʾbati ibni akhī a-turā tajmaʿu al-ayyāmu shamlanā bihi wa-mā naṭlubu al-ijtimāʿa bihi illā mina Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And-when heard the-vizier her-speech, he-rejoiced a-rejoicing intense, and-said: Alas-for-the-longing for the-sight-of the-son-of my-brother! Will-it-be (that) gather the-days our-union with-him? And-not we-seek the-gathering with-him except from God the-Exalted.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard what she said, he was filled with joy, and he said, "Oh, how I long to see my brother's son! Will the days bring us together with him again? We seek that reunion from none but God, the Exalted."
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال (dagger alif: qāla). واشوقاه is a cry of lament or longing, "alas, my longing!"; the final ه is the pausal hāʾ of the exclamation. رؤبة is a misprint for رؤية, "the sight" (ب for ي); I point what is printed. أترى, "I wonder, will it be…?", is the stock interjection (the print's اتري has ي for ى), and takes a bare imperfect. شملنابه is شملنا به run together, "our union with him" (جمع الله شمله is the wish for family reunion). ابن أخي: the vizier calls Badr al-Dīn "my brother's son", his nephew.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ قَامَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ وَخَرَجَ عَلَى الرِّجَالِ الَّذِينَ مَعَهُ وَقَالَ يَمْضِي مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ وَاهْدِمُوهُ وَكَتِّفُوهُ بِعِمَامَتِهِ وَجُرُّوهُ غَصْبًا إِلَى عِنْدِي مِنْ غَيْرِ أَذِيَّةٍ تَحْصُلُلَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra qāma min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi wa-kharaja ʿalā al-rijāli alladhīna maʿahu wa-qāla yamḍī minkum ʿishrūna rajulan dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi wa-ihdimūhu wa-kattifūhu bi-ʿimāmatihi wa-jurrūhu ghaṣban ilā ʿindī min ghayri adhiyyatin taḥṣulu lahu
sentences.l: Then-indeed the-vizier rose from his-time and-his-hour, and-went-out upon the-men who (were) with-him, and-said: Let-go from-among-you twenty (men) (to) the-shop-of the-cook, and-demolish-it, and-bind-him with-his-turban, and-drag-him by-force to my-presence, without harm that-befalls-him.
sentences.i: Then the vizier rose at that very moment and went out to the men who were with him, and said, "Let twenty of you go to the cook's shop and tear it down, and bind him with his own turban and drag him to me by force, but without any harm coming to him."
sentences.n: قام من وقته وساعته, "rose from his time and his hour", is the idiom for "on the spot". يمضي منكم عشرون رجلا is a third-person command ("let twenty go"), and the verb takes its goal as a bare accusative, دكان الطباخ. The print has عشرون in the nominative, which I point as printed. اهدموه is "demolish it", the cook's shop. تحصلله is تحصل له run together, "that befalls him".

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū naʿam
sentences.l: So-they-said: Yes.
sentences.i: They said, "Yes."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ رَكِبَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ إِلَى دَارِالسَّعَادَةِ وَاجْتَمَعَ بِنَائِبِ دِمَشْقَ وَأَطْلَعَهُ عَلَى الْكُتُبِ الَّتِي مَعَهُ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ فَوَضَعَهُمْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ بَعْدَ تَقْلِيبِهِمْ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَأَيْنَ هُوَ غَرِيمُكَ قَالَ رَجُلٌ طَبَّاخٌ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra rakiba min waqtihi ilā dāri al-saʿādati wa-ijtamaʿa bi-nāʾibi dimashqa wa-aṭlaʿahu ʿalā al-kutubi allatī maʿahu mina al-sulṭāni fa-waḍaʿahum ʿalā raʾsihi baʿda taqlībihim wa-qāla lahu wa-ayna huwa gharīmuka qāla rajulun ṭabbākhun
sentences.l: Then-indeed the-vizier rode from his-time to the-house-of the-felicity, and-met with-the-deputy-of Damascus, and-made-him-aware of the-letters which (were) with-him from the-sultan; and-he-placed-them on his-head after turning-them-over; and-said to-him: And-where (is) he, your-adversary? He-said: A-man, a-cook.
sentences.i: Then the vizier rode off at once to the Dār al-Saʿāda and met with the governor of Damascus. He showed him the letters he had with him from the sultan, and the governor put them on his head, after turning them over, and said to him, "And where is this adversary of yours?" He said, "A man, a cook."
sentences.n: دار السعادة, "the House of Felicity", is the governor's residence in Damascus. نائب دمشق, "the deputy of Damascus", is the governor, who acts for the sultan. To put a royal letter on one's head is the gesture of respect paid to it. غريم is a "creditor, adversary", here the man the vizier says he is pursuing.

sentences.t: فَفِى الْحَالِ أَمَرَحُجَّا بِهِ أَنْ يَذْهَبُوا إِلَى دُكَّانِهِ فَذَهَبُوا فَرَأَوْهُ مُهَدَّ وَمَا وَكُلُّ شَيْئٍ فِيهِ مَكْسُورٌ
sentences.tr: fa-fī al-ḥāli amaraḥujjā bihi an yadhhabū ilā dukkānihi fa-dhahabū fa-raʾawhu muhadda wa-mā wa-kullu shayʾin fīhi maksūrun
sentences.l: So-at-the-instant he-commanded the-chamberlains (?) with-it that they-go to his-shop; and-they-went and-saw-it razed (?), and-every thing in-it broken.
sentences.i: At once the governor ordered his chamberlains to go to the cook's shop, and they went and found it razed to the ground, and everything in it smashed.
sentences.n: The print has امرحجا به for what is probably أمر حجّابه, "he ordered his chamberlains" (the word divided oddly); I point أَمَرَ and حُجَّا as printed and give the sense above. مهد وما is obscure and may be corrupt: perhaps مهدوما, "demolished", broken in two by the print; the translation gives only the sense, which the context fixes. شيئ is printed with the precomposed ئ and kept.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُ لَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى دَارِ السَّعَادَةِ فَعَلُوا جَمَاعَتُهُ مَا أَمَرَهُمْ بِهِ فَقَعَدُوا مُنْتَظِرِينَ مَجِىءَ الْوَزِيرِ مِنْ دَارِالسَّعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: li-annahu lammā tawajjaha ilā dāri al-saʿādati faʿalū jamāʿatuhu mā amarahum bihi fa-qaʿadū muntaẓirīna majīʾa al-wazīri min dāri al-saʿādati
sentences.l: Because-he, when he-went-toward the-house-of the-felicity, they-did, his-band, what he-commanded-them with-it; and-they-sat waiting (for) the-coming-of the-vizier from the-house-of the-felicity.
sentences.i: For when the vizier had set out for the Dār al-Saʿāda, his men did what he had commanded them, and then sat waiting for the vizier to come back from the Dār al-Saʿāda.
sentences.n: فعلوا جماعته, "they did, his band", puts the verb in the plural before its subject, which is colloquial; I point جماعته as a nominative in apposition. The subject of توجه, the vizier, is not stated. مجىء is printed with ى followed by a separate ء; it is read majīʾ, "coming".

sentences.t: وَبَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ يَقُولُ يَاتُرَيٰ أَيْشْ رَأَوْا فِي حَبِّ الرُّمَّانِ حَتَّى صَارَ إِلَى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-badru al-dīni ḥasanun yaqūlu yā-turā ayš raʾaw fī ḥabbi al-rummāni ḥattā ṣāra ilā hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: And-Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan saying: I-wonder what they-saw in the-grains-of the-pomegranate that it-came-to this the-affair.
sentences.i: And Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan was saying, "I wonder what they found in the pomegranate seeds, to bring things to this?"
sentences.n: ياتري is يا ترى, "I wonder", the colloquial interjection. أيش is the colloquial "what?" (for أيّ شيء). حتى صار إلى هذا الأمر is "until it came to this state".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَالْوَزِيرُ مِنْ عِنْدِ نَائِبِ دِمَشْقَ وَقَدْ أَذِنَ لَهُ فِي أَخْذِ غَرِيمِهِ وَيُسَافِرَ بِهِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْخِيَامَ طَلَبَ الطَّبَّاخَ فَأَحْضَرُوهُ مُكَتَّفًا بِعِمَامَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara al-wazīru min ʿindi nāʾibi dimashqa wa-qad adhina lahu fī akhdhi gharīmihi wa-yusāfira bihi fa-lammā dakhala al-khiyāma ṭalaba al-ṭabbākha fa-aḥḍarūhu mukattafan bi-ʿimāmatihi
sentences.l: And-when attended the-vizier from at the-deputy-of Damascus, and-he-had been-permitted in taking-of his-adversary and-travelling with-him; and-when he-entered the-tents, he-asked-for the-cook; and-they-brought-him bound with-his-turban.
sentences.i: When the vizier came away from the governor of Damascus, who had given him leave to take his adversary and to travel with him, and entered his tents, he asked for the cook, and they brought him bound with his own turban.
sentences.n: حضرالوزير is حضر الوزير run together. وقد أذن له في أخذ غريمه ويسافر به has no أن before ويسافر; the sense is "to take him and to travel with him", and I point ويسافر as a subjunctive on that reading. الخيام is the vizier's camp, the tents.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ إِلَى عَمِّهِ بَكَي بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara Badru al-Dīni Ḥasanun ilā ʿammihi bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: And-when looked Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan at his-paternal-uncle, he-wept a-weeping intense,
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan looked at his uncle, he wept bitterly,
sentences.n: بدرالدين is printed as one word; I keep it so, with the case ending (here -u) inside it. بكي is printed with ي where Classical writes بكى; it is read bakā, "he wept". The uncle is the vizier, whom Badr al-Dīn now recognises as his father's brother.

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ يَا مَوْلَاىَ مَا ذَنْبِي عِنْدَكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā mawlāya mā dhanbī ʿindakum
sentences.l: And-he-said: O my-master, what (is) my-offence with-you(pl.)?
sentences.i: and he said, "O my master, what is my offence in your eyes?"
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال (dagger alif: qāla); the slip recurs in this slice. عندكم is plural: he addresses the vizier and his men together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي طَبَخْتَ حَبَّ الرُّمَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu anta alladhī ṭabakhta ḥabba al-rummāni
sentences.l: And-said to-him: You (are) the-one-who you-cooked grains-of the-pomegranate?
sentences.i: Then he said to him, "Are you the one who cooked the pomegranate seeds?"
sentences.n: The speaker is the vizier. حب الرمان is the dish of pomegranate seeds that Badr al-Dīn cooked, and left without pepper; this is the offence the vizier goes on to name. There is no question word: the question is carried by tone alone.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ فَأَنْتُمْ وَجَدْتُمْ فِيهِ شَيْءً يُوجِبُ ضَرْبَ الرَّقَبَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam fa-antum wajadtum fīhi shayʾan yūjibu ḍarba al-raqabati
sentences.l: He-said: Yes. So-you(pl.) you-found in-it a-thing necessitating striking-of the-neck?
sentences.i: He said, "Yes. And did you find something in it that calls for the striking-off of a neck?"
sentences.n: Badr al-Dīn is the speaker. شيء is printed with no alif; I give it the accusative it needs as object of وجدتم, with the fatḥatān on the hamza. يوجب follows شيء with no linking word, which is normal for an indefinite noun and its clause. ضرب الرقبة, "striking of the neck", is beheading.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ أَحْسَنُ وَأَقَلُّ جَزَائِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru aḥsanu wa-aqallu jazāʾika
sentences.l: And-said the-vizier: Best and-least (of) your-requital.
sentences.i: The vizier said, "The best, and the least, of your requital."
sentences.n: Terse and elliptic, and I am not sure of it. I read أحسن and أقل as two predicates, "the best and the least of what you are owed", with the sentence left unfinished (what is meant is that the death penalty is the mildest he deserves). Another possibility is أَحْسَنَ as an ironic "well done!"; I keep the first reading.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي مَاتُعَرِّفُنِي بِذَبْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī mā tuʿarrifunī bi-dhabnī
sentences.l: And-said to-him: O my-lord, not you-make-me-know of-my-offence?
sentences.i: Then he said to him, "My lord, will you not tell me my offence?"
sentences.n: ذبني is printed for ذنبي: the ن and ب have changed places, and I point what is printed (dhabnī), reading it as dhanbī, "my offence". ما + imperfect is a negative question, "won't you...?". عَرَّفَ بِـ means "to inform of", and the بِـ introduces the thing made known. The speaker is Badr al-Dīn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ نَعَمْ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru naʿam fī hādhihi al-sāʿati
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-vizier: Yes, in this the-hour.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, "Yes, this very hour."
sentences.n: Elliptic: "yes, (I will tell you) within this hour".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ صَرَخَ عَلَى الْغِلْمَانِ وَقَٰلَ هَاتُوا الْجِمَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra ṣarakha ʿalā al-ghilmāni wa-qāla hātū al-jimāla
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier shouted at the-lads and-said: Bring the-camels.
sentences.i: Then the vizier shouted at his servants and said, "Bring the camels!"
sentences.n: الغلمان are young male servants. I read الجمال as al-jimāl, "camels" (plural of jamal); it could also be al-jammāl, "the camel-drivers", but the camels are what the next lines need. صرخ على is "shout at".

sentences.t: وَأَخَذُوا بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ مَعَهُمْ وَأَدْخَلُوهُ فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَقُفِلَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَارُوا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhū Badra al-Dīni Ḥasana maʿahum wa-adkhalūhu fī ṣundūqin wa-qufila ʿalayhi wa-sārū
sentences.l: And-they-took Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan with-them, and-they-put-him in a-chest, and-it-was-locked upon-him, and-they-journeyed.
sentences.i: They took Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan with them, put him in a chest, locked it on him, and set off.
sentences.n: قفل is printed without vowels; I read it as a passive, qufila, "it was locked", which suits the sentence's change of subject. It could equally be qafala, "he locked".

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ فَحَطُّوا وَأَكَلُوا شَيْئًا مِنَ الطَّعَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna ilā al-layli fa-ḥaṭṭū wa-akalū shayʾan mina al-ṭaʿāmi
sentences.l: And-not they-ceased travelling until the-night; and-they-halted, and-they-ate something of the-food.
sentences.i: They travelled on until night, then halted and ate a little food.
sentences.n: لم يزالوا + a participle means "they kept on doing", and it recurs in this slice. حطوا is colloquial: they "put down" their loads, that is, halted for the night.

sentences.t: وَأَخْرَجُوا بَدْرَالدِّينِ أَطْعَمُوهُ وَعَادُوهُ إِلَى الصُّنْدُوقِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhrajū Badra al-Dīni aṭʿamūhu wa-ʿādūhu ilā al-ṣundūqi
sentences.l: And-they-brought-out Badr al-Dīn, they-fed-him, and-they-returned-him to the-chest.
sentences.i: They brought Badr al-Dīn out, fed him, and put him back in the chest.
sentences.n: أطعموه follows with no "and", as often in this narrative. عادوه is the plain verb عاد used for the causative أعاد, "they put him back"; this is a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا كَذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى قَمْرَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū kadhālika ilā an waṣalū ilā qamrata
sentences.l: And-not they-ceased thus until (that) they-arrived at Qamra.
sentences.i: They went on like this until they came to Qamra.
sentences.n: قمرة is a place-name that I cannot identify from the text alone; I point it as printed, as a name without tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَأَخْرَجُوا بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ وَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي طَبَخْتَ حَبَّ الرُّمَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhrajū Badra al-Dīni Ḥasana mina al-ṣundūqi wa-qāla lahu al-wazīru anta alladhī ṭabakhta ḥabba al-rummāni
sentences.l: And-they-brought-out Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan from the-chest, and-said to-him the-vizier: You (are) the-one-who you-cooked grains-of the-pomegranate?
sentences.i: They brought Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan out of the chest, and the vizier said to him, "Are you the one who cooked the pomegranate seeds?"

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ يَا سَيِّدِي فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ قَيِّدُوهُ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam yā sayyidī fa-qāla al-wazīru qayyidūhu
sentences.l: He-said: Yes, O my-lord. And-said the-vizier: Fetter-him.
sentences.i: He said, "Yes, my lord." Then the vizier said, "Put him in fetters."

sentences.t: فَقَيَّدُوهُ وَعَادُوا بِهِ إِلَى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَسَارُوا إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا مِصْرَوَ قَدْ نَزَلُوا فَى الزَّبْدَانِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qayyadūhu wa-ʿādū bihi ilā al-ṣundūqi wa-sārū ilā an waṣalū miṣra-wa qad nazalū fī al-zabdāniyyati
sentences.l: And-they-fettered-him, and-they-returned with-him to the-chest, and-they-journeyed until they-arrived (at) Egypt, and they-had alighted in al-Zabdāniyya.
sentences.i: So they fettered him, took him back to the chest, and journeyed on until they reached Egypt, and they camped at al-Zabdāniyya.
sentences.n: مصرو is printed as one word. The final و looks like the conjunction "and" run on to the name, before قد نزلوا, and I read it so (miṣra-wa), pointing it with a fatḥa. عادوا بِهِ is "they went back with him": the بِـ means "taking along". الزبدانية is as printed: a place where the party camps on arriving at the city; I cannot say more about it from the text; it may be a corruption of al-Raydāniyya, the open ground outside Cairo where armies camped, but that is a guess.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ بِإِخْرَاجِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ وَأَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ نَجَّارٍ وَقَالَ لَهُ اصْنَعْ لِهَذَ الْعَبَةَ خَشَبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-amara bi-ikhrāji Badri al-Dīni Ḥasanin mina al-ṣundūqi wa-amara bi-iḥḍāri najjārin wa-qāla lahu iṣnaʿ li-hādha al-ʿabata khashabin
sentences.l: And-he-ordered with-the-bringing-out-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan from the-chest, and-ordered with-the-bringing-of a-carpenter, and-said to-him: Make for-this-one the-frame (of) wood.
sentences.i: Then he ordered Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan to be taken out of the chest, and ordered a carpenter to be brought, and said to him, "Make a wooden frame for this one."
sentences.n: أَمَرَ بِـ "order (something)" takes the thing ordered after بِـ; here it is a verbal noun ("the bringing-out"). The last words are obscure. The print has لهذ العبة خشب, and I read it as li-hādha al-laʿba khashab, "for this one the frame of wood", with a lām dropped from اللعبة and the ا of هذا dropped too; the vizier says اللعبة again in the next lines. Treat my pointing of this phrase as a best guess.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَمَا تَصْنَعُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Badru al-Dīni Ḥasanun wa-mā taṣnaʿu bihā
sentences.l: And-said Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: And-what you-make with-it?
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "And what will you do with it?"
sentences.n: صنع بِـ is "do with, do to"; the "it" (feminine) is the frame.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَشْنُقُكَ عَلَيْهَا وَأُسَمِّرُكَ عَلَى اللَّعْبَةِ ثُمَّ أَدُورُ بِكَ الْمَدِينَةَ كُلَّهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ashnuquka ʿalayhā wa-usammiruka ʿalā al-laʿbati thumma adūru bika al-madīnata kullahā
sentences.l: And-he-said: I-hang-you upon-it, and-I-nail-you upon the-frame, then I-go-round with-you the-city all-of-it.
sentences.i: He said, "I will hang you on it and nail you to the frame, and then I will take you round the whole city."
sentences.n: The bare imperfects (أشنقك، أسمرك، أدور) carry the future, as in speech. سَمَّرَ is "to nail"; the vizier means to nail the man to the frame and parade him, and the text does not soften it. لعبة is literally "a plaything"; here it is a contraption, the frame itself. دار بِـ is "to take someone round", and المدينة is accusative as the place gone round.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَلَى أَيِّ شَيْءٍ تَفْعَلُ لِي ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿalā ayyi shayʾin tafʿalu lī dhālika
sentences.l: And-he-said: Upon which thing you-do to-me that?
sentences.i: He said, "On what account do you do that to me?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ عَلَى نَحْسِ طَبْخِكَ حَبَّ الرُّمَّانِ كَيْفَ طَبَخْتَهُ وَهُوَ عَاوِزٌ فُلْفُلٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru ʿalā naḥsi ṭabkhika ḥabba al-rummāni kayfa ṭabakhtahu wa-huwa ʿāwizun fulfulun
sentences.l: And-said the-vizier: For the-ill-luck-of your-cooking grains-of the-pomegranate! How you-cooked it, and-it (is) wanting pepper?
sentences.i: The vizier said, "For your wretched cooking of the pomegranate seeds! How could you cook it when it lacks pepper?"
sentences.n: عاوز is colloquial (Egyptian) for "wanting, needing"; here the dish is "in need of pepper", that is, it was cooked without any. I point it and the following noun as printed, as bare nominatives. نحس, "ill-luck, wretchedness", is the vizier's contemptuous word for the cooking.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَلِكَوْنِهِ عَاوِزٌ فُلْفُلٌ تَصْنَعُ مَعِي هَذَا كُلَّهُ وَمَا كَفَاكَ حَبْسِي وَكُلَّ يَوْمٍ تُطْعِمُونِي أَكْلَةً وَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-li-kawnihi ʿāwizun fulfulun taṣnaʿu maʿī hādhā kullahu wa-mā kafāka ḥabsī wa-kulla yawmin tuṭʿimūnī aklatan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: And-because-of-its-being wanting pepper, you-do with-me this all-of-it? And-not sufficed-you my-imprisonment, and-every day you(pl.)-feed-me one meal?
sentences.i: He said to him, "And because it lacked pepper, you do all this to me? Was it not enough for you to imprison me, and feed me only one meal a day?"
sentences.n: ولكونه is وَ + لِـ + كَوْن + ـهِ, "and because of its being"; the لِـ gives the reason. صنع مَعَ is "to do with", that is, "to do to". تطعموني is plural, so he speaks to the vizier and his men together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ عَاوِزٌ فُلْفُلٌ وَمَا جَزَاؤُكَ إِلَّا الْقَتْلُ فَتَعَجَّبَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ وَحَزِنَ عَلَى رُوحِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru ʿāwizun fulfulun wa-mā jazāʾuka illā al-qatlu fa-taʿajjaba Badru al-Dīni wa-ḥazina ʿalā rūḥihi
sentences.l: And-said the-vizier: Wanting pepper! And-not (is) your-requital except the-killing. And-marvelled Badr al-Dīn, and-grieved over his-spirit.
sentences.i: The vizier said, "It lacks pepper, does it? Your only requital is death." Badr al-Dīn was amazed, and grieved for himself.
sentences.n: The vizier repeats the dish's fault with scorn. حزن عَلَى رُوحِهِ is "he grieved for himself": روح, "spirit", is used colloquially for the self.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ فِيمَا تُفَكِّرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru fīmā tufakkiru
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-vizier: In-what you-reflect?
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, "What are you thinking about?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ فِى الْعُقُولِ الْقِشْرَوِيَّةِ الَّتِي مِثْلُ عَقْلِكَ فَإِنَّهُ لَوْكَانَ عِنْدَكَ عَقْلٌ مَاكُنْتَ فَعَلْتَ مَعِي هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu fī al-ʿuqūli al-qishrawiyyati allatī mithlu ʿaqlika fa-innahu law-kāna ʿindaka ʿaqlun mā-kunta faʿalta maʿī hādhihi al-fiʿāla
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: In the-minds the-husk-like which (are) like-your-mind; for-indeed-it, if-there-were with-you a-mind, you-would-not have-done with-me these the-deeds.
sentences.i: He said to him, "I am thinking of shallow minds like yours. For if you had any sense, you would not have done these things to me."
sentences.n: القشروية is from قشر, "rind, husk, shell", and the ـَوِيَّة ending is colloquial: a mind that is all husk and no kernel, so "shallow". فإنه لو كان... ما كنت فعلت is the "if... would not have" pattern; فإنه is just a linking "for indeed". هذه الفعال is for هذه الأفعال, with the colloquial plural فِعَال of فِعْل, "deed".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نُؤْذِيَكَ حَتَّى لَا تَعُودَ لِمِثْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru yajibu ʿalaynā an nuʾdhiyaka ḥattā lā taʿūda li-mithlihi
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-vizier: It-is-incumbent upon-us that we-hurt-you until not you-return to-the-like-of-it.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, "We are bound to hurt you, so that you never go back to the like of it."
sentences.n: The print has نوذيك with no hamza sign; it is nuʾdhīka, "we hurt you", and the hamza is mine. يجب عَلَى is "it is incumbent on".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ إِنَّ الَّذِي فَعَلْتَهُ مَعِي أَقَلُّ شَيْءٍ فِيهِ أَذِيَّتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Badru al-Dīni Ḥasanun inna alladhī faʿaltahu maʿī aqallu shayʾin fīhi adhiyyatī
sentences.l: And-said Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: Indeed that-which you-did with-me, the-least thing in-it (is) my-hurt.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "What you have done to me: the least part of it is the hurt it does me."
sentences.n: Compressed: أقل شيء فيه, "the least thing in it", is the minimum, and the minimum is already an injury. The antecedent الذي فعلته is left hanging as the topic of the sentence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ شَنْقِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu lā budda min shanqika
sentences.l: And-said to-him: No escape from hanging-you.
sentences.i: He said to him, "There is no avoiding your hanging."

sentences.t: كُلَّ هَذَا وَالنَّجَّارُ يُصْلِحُ الْخَشَبَ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا كَذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: kulla hādhā wa-al-najjāru yuṣliḥu al-khashaba wa-huwa yanẓuru wa-lam yazālū kadhālika ilā an aqbala al-laylu
sentences.l: All this, while the-carpenter (was) preparing the-wood, and-he (was) looking; and-not they-ceased thus until came-on the-night.
sentences.i: All this while the carpenter was getting the timber ready and Badr al-Dīn looked on; and so they went on until night came.
sentences.n: I read كل هذا as "all this (while)", the accusative of duration, and what follows as a circumstantial clause (وَالنَّجَّارُ يُصْلِحُ... وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ), "the carpenter getting ready... and he watching". The "he" is Badr al-Dīn.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُ عَمُّهُ وَرَمَاهُ فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَقَالَ فِي غَدٍيَكُونُ الْأَمْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahu ʿammuhu wa-ramāhu fī al-ṣundūqi wa-qāla fī ghadin yakūnu al-amru
sentences.l: And-took-him his-uncle and-threw-him into the-chest, and-said: In tomorrow will-be the-matter.
sentences.i: Then his uncle took him and threw him into the chest, and said, "Tomorrow the business will be done."
sentences.n: غديكون is two words run together, غَدٍ and يَكُونُ, and I keep the print's spacing. في غد is "tomorrow"; الأمر, "the matter", is the business in hand, the hanging he has just announced (though the uncle's real plan is the opposite, as the next lines show).

sentences.t: وَصَبَرَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى عَرَفَ أَنَّهُ نَامَ فَقَامَ وَحَمَلَ الصُّنْدُوقَ وَرَكِبَ وَحَطَّهُ قُدَّامَهُ وَدَخَلَ الْمَدِينَةَ وَسَارَ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣabara ʿalayhi ḥattā ʿarafa annahu nāma fa-qāma wa-ḥamala al-ṣundūqa wa-rakiba wa-ḥaṭṭahu quddāmahu wa-dakhala al-madīnata wa-sāra ilā an dakhala baytahu
sentences.l: And-he-was-patient with-him until he-knew that-he slept; and-he-rose, and-carried the-chest, and-rode, and-put-it before-him, and-entered the-city, and-went until he-entered his-house.
sentences.i: He waited for him until he knew he was asleep; then he got up, took up the chest, mounted, set it in front of him, rode into the city, and went on until he came to his house.
sentences.n: صبر عَلَى is "to be patient with, to wait for". قدامه is colloquial for "in front of him", the chest being propped before him on the saddle. The "he" throughout is the vizier.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِا بْنَتِهِ سِتِّ الْحُسْنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَمَعَ شَمْلَكِ بِابْنِ عَمِّكِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-i bnatihi sitti al-ḥusni al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī jamaʿa shamlaki bi-ibni ʿammiki
sentences.l: Then he-said to his-daughter Sitt al-Ḥusn: The-praise (is) to-God who gathered your-union with-the-son-of your-paternal-uncle.
sentences.i: Then he said to his daughter, Sitt al-Ḥusn, "Praise be to God, who has brought you together again with your cousin!"
sentences.n: لا بنته is printed as two words, the لـ detached from ابنته; I keep the print's spacing and read li-ibnatihi, "to his daughter". جمع شمله is an idiom: "he gathered his scattered state", that is, he reunited. ابن عمك, "your paternal uncle's son", is the usual word for "cousin" and for a cousin as a husband.

sentences.t: قُومِي اِفْرُشِى الْبَيْتَ مِثْلَ نَصْبَتِهِ لَيْلَةَ الْجِلَاءِ
sentences.tr: qūmī ifrushī al-bayta mithla naṣbatihi laylata al-jilāʾi
sentences.l: Rise; spread the-house like its-arrangement (on) the-night-of the-unveiling.
sentences.i: "Get up and furnish the house as it was arranged on the night of the unveiling."
sentences.n: قومي افرشي has no "and" between the two commands. فرش is "to spread", and so "to lay carpets and furnish". الجلاء is the night the bride is displayed, that is, the wedding night; I point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَامُوا أَوْقَدُوا الشُّمُوعَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmū awqadū al-shumūʿa
sentences.l: And-they-rose, they-lit the-candles.
sentences.i: They got up and lit the candles.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَخْرَجَ الْوَزِيرُ الْوَرَقَةَ الْمُصَوَّرَةَ الَّتِي كَانَ صَوَّرَهَا بِنَصْبَةِ الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad akhraja al-wazīru al-waraqata al-muṣawwarata allatī kāna ṣawwarahā bi-naṣbati al-bayti
sentences.l: And-already brought-out the-vizier the-sheet the-drawn which he-had drawn-it with-the-arrangement-of the-house
sentences.i: The vizier had brought out the sheet he had drawn, showing how the house was arranged,
sentences.n: الورقة المصورة is "the sheet with a drawing on it": the vizier had made a plan of the room. The بِـ in بنصبة البيت is "with, showing"; a sheet drawn "with the arrangement of the house".

sentences.t: وَ وَضَعُوا كُلَّ شَىْ مَكَانَهُ حَتَّى أَنَّ الرَّائِيَ إِذَارَأَي ذَلِكَ لَايَشُكُّ فِي أَنَّهَا لَيْلَةُ الْجِلَاءِ بِعَيْنِهَا
sentences.tr: wa waḍaʿū kulla shay makānahu ḥattā anna al-rāʾiya idhā-raʾā dhālika lā-yashukku fī annahā laylatu al-jilāʾi bi-ʿaynihā
sentences.l: And they-placed every thing (in) its-place, until that the-beholder, when-he-saw that, not-doubts that-it (is) the-night-of the-unveiling with-its-own-self.
sentences.i: and they put everything in its place, so that anyone who saw it would have had no doubt that it was the very night of the unveiling.
sentences.n: The print leaves a lone و at the end of the line before وضعوا; it is the "and" of the verb, and I keep the split. شى is the print's spelling of شيء, read shay with no hamza (colloquial). اذاراي and لايشك are each printed as one word; بعينها is "with its very eye", an idiom for "itself, exactly".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الْوَزِيرُ أَنْ يَحُطُّوا شَاشَ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ فِي مَكَانِهِ كَمَا كَانَ حَطَّهُ بِيَدِهِ وَكَذَلِكَ السِّرْوَالَ وَالْكِيسَ الَّذِي تَحْتَ الطَّرَّاحَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-wazīru an yaḥuṭṭū shāsha Badri al-Dīni Ḥasanin fī makānihi kamā kāna ḥaṭṭahu bi-yadihi wa-kadhālika al-sirwāla wa-al-kīsa alladhī taḥta al-ṭarrāḥati
sentences.l: Then ordered the-vizier that they-put the-muslin-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan in its-place as he-had put-it with-his-hand, and-likewise the-trousers and-the-purse which (is) under the-mattress.
sentences.i: Then the vizier ordered them to put Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan's turban-cloth in its place, just as he had laid it with his own hand, and likewise the trousers and the purse that was under the mattress.
sentences.n: الشاش is the muslin wound round a cap as a turban. The turban-cloth, the trousers and the purse are the things Badr al-Dīn left behind on that earlier night, and the vizier is setting the stage so that he will take it for the same night. حط is colloquial "to put, lay down".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَمَرَا بِنْتَهُ أَنْ تُخَفِّفَ نَفْسَهَا كَمَا كَانَتْ لَيْلَةَ الْجَلَاءِ فِي الْخَلْوَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra amarā bintahu an tukhaffifa nafsahā kamā kānat laylata al-jalāʾi fī al-khalwati
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier ordered his-daughter that she-lighten her-self as she-was (on) the-night-of the-unveiling in the-seclusion.
sentences.i: Then the vizier told his daughter to put herself at ease, just as she had been on the night of the unveiling, in private.
sentences.n: أَمَرَا is printed with a final alif after the verb; read amara, "he ordered", and take the alif as a spelling slip. تُخَفِّفَ نَفْسَهَا is literally "lighten herself"; it may mean "put herself at ease" or "make herself light (of her finery)", and I cannot decide between them, so I keep the literal wording and a neutral English sense. الْجَلَاء is the unveiling of the bride to the groom, the high point of the wedding night.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْكِ ابْنُ عَمِّكِ فَقُولِي لَهُ أَبْطَأْتَ عَلَيَّ فِي عُبُورِكَ بَيْتَ الْخَلَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā idhā dakhala ʿalayki ibnu ʿammiki fa-qūlī lahu abṭaʾta ʿalayya fī ʿubūrika bayta al-khalāʾi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: When he-enters upon-you son-of your-paternal-uncle, then-say to-him: You-were-slow upon-me in your-crossing house-of the-privy.
sentences.i: And he said to her, "When your cousin comes in to you, say to him, 'You kept me waiting while you went to the privy.'"
sentences.n: ابْنُ عَمِّكِ, "son of your paternal uncle", is the ordinary word for a (male) cousin; here it is Badr al-Dīn. أَبْطَأْتَ عَلَيَّ, "you were slow upon me", means "you kept me waiting". بَيْتَ الْخَلَاءِ, "the house of emptiness", is the privy; it stands in the accusative as the place crossed to, so "your crossing (to) the privy".

sentences.t: وَدَعِيهِ يَبَاتَ عِنْدَكِ وَتُحَدِّثِينَ مَعَهُ إِلَى النَّهَارِ نَكْشِفُ لَهُ هَذَا التَّارِيخَ
sentences.tr: wa-daʿīhi yabāta ʿindaki wa-tuḥaddithīna maʿahu ilā al-nahāri nakshifu lahu hādhā al-tārīkha
sentences.l: And-leave-him he-spend-the-night with-you, and-you-converse with-him until the-day; we-uncover to-him this the-history.
sentences.i: Let him spend the night with you, and talk with him until daybreak; then we shall reveal to him this whole story.
sentences.n: يَبَاتَ is printed with a long ā, a colloquial form of the Classical يَبِيتَ, "spend the night"; and after دَعِيهِ, "let him", no connecting word is needed. The final clause نَكْشِفُ لَهُ simply follows the previous with no "so that"; it reads "(so that) we may uncover". التَّارِيخ is "history, account"; here the whole story of the affair.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَخْرَجَ بَدْرَالدِّينِ مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ بَعْدَ أَنْ فَكَّ الْقَيْدَ مِنْ رِجْلَيْهِ وَقَلَعَهُ مَا عَلَيْهِ وَصَارَ بِقَمِيصِ النَّوْمِ وَهُوَ زَفِيعٌ مِنْ غَيْرِ سِرْوَالٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra akhraja badra al-dīni mina al-ṣundūqi baʿda an fakka al-qayda min rijlayhi wa-qalaʿahu mā ʿalayhi wa-ṣāra bi-qamīṣi al-nawmi wa-huwa zafīʿun min ghayri sirwālin
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier brought-out Badr al-Dīn from the-chest, after he-loosed the-fetter from his-two-legs, and-stripped-him (of) what (was) upon-him; and-he-became in-shirt-of the-sleep, and-he zafīʿ, without trousers.
sentences.i: Then the vizier took Badr al-Dīn out of the chest, after loosing the fetter from his legs and stripping him of what he wore, so that he was left in his nightshirt, bare and without trousers.
sentences.n: قَلَعَهُ مَا عَلَيْهِ takes two objects: he "stripped him (of) what was on him". زَفِيع I cannot find in Lane or Hava; the words that follow, "without trousers", make the sense plain enough ("stripped, bare"), but treat my pointing as a guess at an obscure or corrupt word. قَمِيص النَّوْم is the "sleeping-shirt", the nightshirt.

sentences.t: كُلُّ هَذَا وَهُوَ نَائِمٌ لَا يَعْلَمُ
sentences.tr: kullu hādhā wa-huwa nāʾimun lā yaʿlamu
sentences.l: All this, and-he asleep, not he-knows.
sentences.i: All this happened while he slept, knowing nothing of it.

sentences.t: فَبِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ انْقَلَبَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ تَنَبَّهَ فَوَجَدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي دِهْلِيزِ نُورٍ فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ أَنَا فِي أَضْغَاثِ أَحْلَامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-bi-al-amri al-muqaddari inqalaba badru al-dīni tanabbaha fa-wajada nafsahu fī dihlīzi nūrin fa-qāla fī nafsihi anā fī aḍghāthi aḥlāmin
sentences.l: So by the-matter the-decreed, turned-over Badr al-Dīn, awoke, and-found his-self in vestibule-of light; and-said in his-self: I (am) in muddles-of dreams.
sentences.i: Then, by decree of fate, Badr al-Dīn turned over and woke, and found himself in a lighted vestibule; and he said to himself, "I am caught in a jumble of dreams."
sentences.n: انْقَلَبَ تَنَبَّهَ puts two verbs side by side with no "and": he "turned over, woke". الْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ is "the decreed matter", fate; بِـ here means "by". دِهْلِيزِ نُورٍ I read as "a vestibule of light", a lit passage, but نُور could also be a name; the print gives no help. أَضْغَاث أَحْلَام, "bundles (of mixed stalks) of dreams", is the stock phrase for confused, meaningless dreams.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ تَمَشَّى قَلِيلًا إِلَى بَابٍ ثَانٍ وَنَظَرَ وَإِذَا هُوَ فِى الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي انْجَلَتْ فِيهِ عَلَيْهِ الْعَرُوسَةُ الْبَشْخَانَهْ وَالْكُرْسِيِّ
sentences.tr: thumma qāma badru al-dīni tamashshā qalīlan ilā bābin thānin wa-naẓara wa-idhā huwa fī al-bayti alladhī injalat fīhi ʿalayhi al-ʿarūsatu al-bashkhānah wa-al-kursiyyi
sentences.l: Then rose Badr al-Dīn, walked a-little to a-door second, and-looked, and-behold he (was) in the-house in-which was-unveiled to-him the-bride, the-bashkhana and-the-chair.
sentences.i: Then Badr al-Dīn got up and walked a little way to a second door, and looked, and found he was in the house where the bride had been unveiled to him, with the bashkhana and the chair.
sentences.n: تَمَشَّى follows قَامَ with no "and": "rose, walked". The last two words, الْبَشْخَانَهْ وَالْكُرْسِيِّ, I read as naming the setting of the unveiling, in apposition to "the house"; they could also be read as things he now sees. The print has ه for ة in الْبَشْخَانَهْ, pointed as a pausal -ah. بَشْخَانَة is a Persian-derived word for a canopied alcove or chamber, and its exact sense is uncertain. وَإِذَا هُوَ means "and behold, he was".

sentences.t: وَنَظَرَ عِمَامَتَهُ وَحَوَائِجَهُ فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ ذَلِكَ بَهِتَ وَصَارَ يُقَدِّمُ رِجْلًا وَيُؤَخِّرُ أُخْرَى
sentences.tr: wa-naẓara ʿimāmatahu wa-ḥawāʾijahu fa-lammā naẓara dhālika bahita wa-ṣāra yuqaddimu rijlan wa-yuʾakhkhiru ukhrā
sentences.l: And-he-looked-at his-turban and-his-needs; and-when he-saw that, he-was-dumbfounded, and-came-to-be advancing a-foot and-putting-back another.
sentences.i: He saw his turban and his belongings, and when he saw them he was struck dumb, and he went along moving one foot forward and drawing the other back.
sentences.n: حَوَائِج are one's "needs" and so, by extension, one's things and belongings. بَهِتَ means "was dumbfounded, struck dumb".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَنَا نَائِمٌ أَمْ يَقْظَانُ وَصَارَ يَمْسَحُ جَبِينَهُ وَيَقُولُ وَهُوَ مُتَعَجِّبٌ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا مَكَانُ الْعَرُوسَةِ الَّتِي انْجَلَتْ عَلَيَّ فَأَنَا فَيْنْ فَإِنِّي كُنْتُ فِي صُنْدُوقٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla anā nāʾimun am yaqẓānu wa-ṣāra yamsaḥu jabīnahu wa-yaqūlu wa-huwa mutaʿajjibun wa-Allāhi inna hādhā makānu al-ʿarūsati allatī injalat ʿalayya fa-anā fayn fa-innī kuntu fī ṣundūqin
sentences.l: And-he-said: I asleep or awake? And-came-to-be wiping his-forehead, and-saying, and-he marvelling: By-God, indeed this (is) place-of the-bride who was-unveiled upon-me! So-I where? For-indeed-I was in a-chest!
sentences.i: And he said, "Am I asleep or awake?" and he began to wipe his forehead, and said in amazement, "By God, this is the place of the bride who was unveiled to me! Then where am I? For I was in a chest!"
sentences.n: فَيْن is colloquial for "where" (Egyptian fēn, from فِي + أَيْن); it is why the Arabic reads "so I, where?" with no verb. يَقْظَان is "awake" (a diptote).

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يُخَاطِبُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِذَا بِسِتِّ الْحُسْنِ رَفَعَتْ ذَيْلَ الْبَشْخَانَةِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا تَدْخُلُ فَإِنَّكَ أَبْطَأْتَ فِي بَيْتِ الْخَلَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa yukhāṭibu nafsahu wa-idhā bi-sitti al-ḥusni rafaʿat dhayla al-bashkhānati wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī mā tadkhulu fa-innaka abṭaʾta fī bayti al-khalāʾi
sentences.l: So-while he addressing his-self, and-behold with-Sitt al-Ḥusn (who) raised the-hem-of the-bashkhana, and-said to-him: O my-lord, not you-enter? For-indeed-you were-slow in house-of the-privy.
sentences.i: While he was talking to himself, behold, Sitt al-Ḥusn lifted the hem of the bashkhana and said to him, "My lord, won't you come in? You have been a long time in the privy."
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِ... "and behold (there appeared)": the بِـ after إِذَا marks what suddenly appears. سِتّ is "lady", so Sitt al-Ḥusn is "Lady of Beauty". ذَيْلَ الْبَشْخَانَةِ, "the hem of the bashkhana", suggests that here the word means a curtain or canopy. مَا تَدْخُلُ is colloquial: "won't you come in? why don't you come in?".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَهَا وَنَظَرَ إِلَى وَجْهِهَا ضَحِكَ وَقَٰلَ إِتْنِي فِي أَضْغَاثِ أَحْلَامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāmahā wa-naẓara ilā wajhihā ḍaḥika wa-qāla itnī fī aḍghāthi aḥlāmin
sentences.l: And-when he-heard her-speech and-looked at her-face, he-laughed and-said: Itnī in muddles-of dreams.
sentences.i: When he heard her words and looked at her face, he laughed and said, "I am in a jumble of dreams."
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال; the dagger alif marks the long ā, as in the other places where it appears below. اتني is surely a slip for إنني or إني, "I am" (ت for ن); I point the letters as printed, as إِتْنِي, and the English gives the sense that the context requires.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ وَتَنَهَّدَ وَتَفَكَّرَ فِيمَا جَرَى لَهُ وَتَحَيَّرَ فِي أَمْرِهِ وَأَشْكَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ قَضِينَهُ لَمَّا رَأَى شَاشَهُ وَسِرْوَالَهُ وَالْكِيسَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala wa-tanahhada wa-tafakkara fī-mā jarā lahu wa-taḥayyara fī amrihi wa-ashkalat ʿalayhi qaḍīnahu lammā raʾā shāshahu wa-sirwālahu wa-al-kīsa alladhī fīhi al-alfu dīnārin
sentences.l: Then he-entered, and-sighed, and-reflected on what happened to-him, and-was-bewildered in his-affair, and-became-confused upon-him his-case when he-saw his-turban-cloth and-his-trousers and-the-purse which in-it the-thousand dinar.
sentences.i: Then he went in, sighed, thought over what had happened to him, and was bewildered about his situation; and his case grew all the more tangled for him when he saw his turban-cloth, his trousers, and the purse with the thousand dinars in it.
sentences.n: قَضِينَهُ is printed with ن where قَضِيَّتُهُ, "his case, his affair", would have ت; I take it as that word and point the letters as printed. أَشْكَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ means "became ambiguous, perplexing to him". الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ, with the article on the number, is simply "the thousand dinars". شَاش is the muslin of the turban.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ إِنِّي فِي أَضْغَاثِ أَحْلَامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Allāhu aʿlamu innī fī aḍghāthi aḥlāmin
sentences.l: And-he-said: God (is) most-knowing; indeed-I (am) in muddles-of dreams.
sentences.i: He said, "God knows best; I am surely in a jumble of dreams."

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ لَهُ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ مَالَكَ تَتَعَجَّبُ وَتَبْهَتُ وَقَالَتْ مَا كُنْتَ كَذَا أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qālat lahu sittu al-ḥusni mālaka tataʿajjabu wa-tabhatu wa-qālat mā kunta kadhā awwala al-layli
sentences.l: So at that said to-him Sitt al-Ḥusn: What-(is) to-you (that) you-marvel and-are-dumbfounded? And-she-said: You-were not thus (at) the-first-of the-night.
sentences.i: At that Sitt al-Ḥusn said to him, "What is the matter with you, that you marvel and stand dumbfounded?" And she said, "You were not like this at the beginning of the night."
sentences.n: مَالَكَ, "what (is) to you?", means "what is wrong with you?", and the verbs that follow are an unconnected clause saying what is wrong.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ وَقَالَ كَمْ لِي غَائِبٌ عَنْكِ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ سَلَامَتَكَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ حَوَالَيْكَ أَنْتَ خَرَجْتَ تَقْضِي لَكَ شُغْلًا وَتَرْجِعُ فَأَنْتَ عَدِمَ عَقْلُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika wa-qāla kam lī ghāʾibun ʿanki fa-qālat lahu salāmataka ismu Allāhi ḥawālayka anta kharajta taqḍī laka shughlan wa-tarjiʿu fa-anta ʿadima ʿaqluka
sentences.l: So he-laughed and-said: How-long to-me absent from-you? And-she-said to-him: Your-safety! The-name-of God (be) around-you! You went-out (to) fulfil for-you a-matter and-return, and-you: gone (is) your-mind.
sentences.i: He laughed and said, "How long have I been away from you?" She said to him, "Your safety! God's name be around you! You only went out to see to your business and come back, and now your wits are gone."
sentences.n: كَمْ لِي غَائِبٌ is colloquial: "how long (is it) that I (have been) absent?". سَلَامَتَكَ ("your safety!") and اسْمُ اللَّهِ حَوَالَيْكَ ("God's name around you") are reassuring formulas, here said half in alarm and half to ward off the evil eye. عَدِمَ عَقْلُكَ is "your mind has gone, is lost", with the subject after the verb. تَقْضِي لَكَ شُغْلًا is "to settle a matter for yourself"; the verb has no connecting word, which is characteristic of this register.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ ذَلِكَ ضَحِكَ وَقَالَ صَدَقْتِ وَلَكِنْ لَمَّا خَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِكِ نَسِيتُ رُوحِى عَلَى بَيْتِ الْمَاءِ وَحَلَمْتُ أَنِّي كُنْتُ طَبَّاخًا فِي دِمَشْقَ وَأَقَمْتُ بِهَا عَشْرَ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa badru al-dīni dhālika ḍaḥika wa-qāla ṣadaqti wa-lākin lammā kharajtu min ʿindiki nasītu rūḥī ʿalā bayti al-māʾi wa-ḥalamtu annī kuntu ṭabbākhan fī dimashqa wa-aqamtu bihā ʿashra sinīna
sentences.l: And-when heard Badr al-Dīn that, he-laughed and-said: You-spoke-truly; but when I-went-out from with-you, I-forgot my-spirit at house-of the-water, and-I-dreamed that-I was a-cook in Damascus, and-I-stayed in-it ten years.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn heard that, he laughed and said, "You are right; but when I went out from you, I lost myself in the privy, and I dreamed that I was a cook in Damascus and stayed there ten years."
sentences.n: نَسِيتُ رُوحِى عَلَى is "I forgot my self at", that is, lost track of myself. بَيْت الْمَاء, "the house of water", is another name for the privy. رُوحِى is printed with ى for ي.

sentences.t: وَكَأَنِّي جَاءَنِي صَغِيرٌ وَهُوَ مِنْ أَوْلَادِ الْأَكَابِرِ وَمَعَهُ خَادِمٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ka-annī jāʾanī ṣaghīrun wa-huwa min awlādi al-akābiri wa-maʿahu khādimun
sentences.l: And-as-though-I came-to-me a-small-one, and-he (was) of sons-of the-great-ones, and-with-him a-servant.
sentences.i: And it seemed that a youth came to me, one of the sons of the great, with a servant at his side.
sentences.n: كَأَنِّي, "as if I", is used here to introduce what he dreamed or half-remembers; the construction recurs below. صَغِير is "small one", a boy or youth.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ مَسَّ بِيَدِهِ عَلَى جَبِينِهِ فَرَأَى الضَّرْبَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ يَاسِتِّي كَأَنَّهُ حَقٌّلِأَنَّهُ ضَرَبَنِي عَلَى جَبِينِي فَشَجَّهُ فَكَأَنَّهُ فِى الْيَقَظَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna badra al-dīni ḥasana massa bi-yadihi ʿalā jabīnihi fa-raʾā al-ḍarba ʿalayhi fa-qāla wa-Allāhi yā sitti ka-annahu ḥaqqun li-annahu ḍarabanī ʿalā jabīnī fa-shajjahu fa-ka-annahu fī al-yaqaẓati
sentences.l: Then indeed Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan touched with-his-hand upon his-forehead, and-saw the-blow upon-it, and-said: By-God, O-my-lady, as-though-it true because-he struck-me upon my-forehead and-split-it; so as-though-it (was) in the-wakefulness.
sentences.i: Then Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan touched his forehead with his hand and found the mark of the blow on it, and said, "By God, my lady, it seems to be true, for he struck me on the forehead and split it; so it seems it was in waking life."
sentences.n: The print runs حقلانه together; I read it as حَقٌّ, "true", plus لِأَنَّهُ, "because he", and have left the letters unspaced as printed. فَرَأَى الضَّرْبَ عَلَيْهِ is "he saw the blow (its mark) on it". شَجَّهُ is "split, wounded his head".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ كَأَنَّهُ مِنْ سَاعَةٍ مَاتَعَانَقْتُ أَنَا وَأَنْتِ وَنِمْنَا فَكَأَنِّي رَأَيْتُهُ فِي الْمَنَامِ وَرَأَيْتُ كَأَنِّي سَافَرْتُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ بِلَا طَرْبُوشٍ وَلَاسِرْوَالٍ وَعَمِلْتُ طَبَّاخًا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla ka-annahu min sāʿatin mā taʿānaqtu anā wa-anti wa-nimnā fa-ka-annī raʾaytuhu fī al-manāmi wa-raʾaytu ka-annī sāfartu ilā dimashqa bi-lā ṭarbūshin wa-lā-sirwālin wa-ʿamiltu ṭabbākhan
sentences.l: Then he-said: As-though-it (is) from an-hour since I-embraced, I and-you, and-we-slept; and-as-though-I saw-it in the-sleep, and-I-saw as-though-I travelled to Damascus without tarbush and-no-trousers, and-I-worked (as) a-cook.
sentences.i: Then he said, "It seems it is only an hour since you and I embraced and slept; and it was as though I saw it in sleep: I saw myself travelling to Damascus without a tarbush and without trousers, and working as a cook."
sentences.n: مَاتَعَانَقْتُ أَنَا وَأَنْتِ has a singular verb ("I embraced") followed by "I and you", where Classical would use the plural تَعَانَقْنَا; مِنْ سَاعَةٍ مَا, "from an hour since", is "only an hour ago". The print joins مَا to the verb and لَا to سِرْوَالٍ. عَمِلْتُ طَبَّاخًا is "I worked (as) a cook", with the job as a bare accusative. طَرْبُوش is the fez.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَهِتَ سَاعَةً وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ كَأَنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَنِّي طَبَخْتُ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ وَفُلْفُلُهُ قَلِيلٌ وَاللَّهِ مَاكَأَنِّي إِلَّا نِمْتُ فِي بَيْتِ الْمَاءِ وَرَأَيْتُ هَذَا كُلَّهُ فِى الْمَنَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma bahita sāʿatan wa-qāla wa-Allāhi ka-annī raʾaytu annī ṭabakhtu ḥabba rummānin wa-fulfuluhu qalīlun wa-Allāhi mā-ka-annī illā nimtu fī bayti al-māʾi wa-raʾaytu hādhā kullahu fī al-manāmi
sentences.l: Then he-was-dumbfounded an-hour, and-said: By-God, as-though-I saw that-I cooked seeds-of pomegranate, and-its-pepper (was) little. By-God, not-as-though-I (was) except (that) I-slept in house-of the-water and-saw this all-of-it in the-sleep.
sentences.i: Then he stood dumbfounded for a while and said, "By God, I seem to have seen myself cooking pomegranate seeds, with very little pepper in them. By God, all I did was sleep in the privy and see all this in a dream."
sentences.n: حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ, "seeds of pomegranate", is the dish he cooked in the dream. مَاكَأَنِّي إِلَّا نِمْتُ, "it is as if I only slept", means "nothing happened but that I slept".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَأَيْشَ رَأَيْتَ زِيَادَةً عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَحَكَى لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu sittu al-ḥusni bi-Allāhi ʿalayka wa-aysha raʾayta ziyādatan ʿalā dhālika fa-ḥakā lahā
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him, Sitt al-Ḥusn: By-God upon-you! And-what did-you-see (as) addition upon that? And-he-related to-her.
sentences.i: Sitt al-Ḥusn said to him, "For God's sake, what more did you see beyond that?" And he told her.
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ, "by God, upon you", is a plea: "I beg you". أَيْش is colloquial "what", from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَاللَّهِ لَوْلَا أَنِّي تَنَبَّهْتُ لَكَانُوا سَمَّرُونِي عَلَى لُعْبَةِ خَشَبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-Allāhi lawlā annī tanabbahtu la-kānū sammarūnī ʿalā luʿbati khashabin
sentences.l: So at that said Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: By-God, were-it-not that-I awoke, they-would-have they-nailed-me onto a-toy-of wood.
sentences.i: Then Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "By God, if I had not woken up, they would have nailed me to a wooden toy."
sentences.n: لَكَانُوا سَمَّرُونِي, with كَانَ plus a perfect, is a colloquial way of saying "they would have nailed me". لُعْبَة خَشَب, "a wooden toy", is his scornful name for the wooden frame on which he was to be hanged.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ عَلَى أَيْشَ فَقَالَ عَلَى قِلَّةِ فُلْفُلِ حَبِّ الرُّمَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ʿalā aysha fa-qāla ʿalā qillati fulfuli ḥabbi al-rummāni
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: Upon what? And-he-said: Upon scarcity-of pepper-of seeds-of the-pomegranate.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Over what?" And he said, "Over too little pepper in the pomegranate seeds."

sentences.t: وَ كَأَنَّهُمْ خَرَّبُوا دُكَّانِي وَكَسَّرُوا مَوَاعِينِي وَحَطُّونِي فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَجَاوُأ بِالنَّجَّارِ يَصْنَعُ لِي خَشَبَةً لِأَنَّهُمْ أَرَادُوا شَنْقِي
sentences.tr: wa ka-annahum kharrabū dukkānī wa-kassarū mawāʿīnī wa-ḥaṭṭūnī fī ṣundūqin wa-jāʾū bi-al-najjāri yaṣnaʿu lī khashabatan li-annahum arādū shanqī
sentences.l: And as-though-they wrecked my-shop, and-smashed my-vessels, and-put-me in a-chest, and-came with-the-carpenter (that) he-make for-me a-plank, because-they wanted my-hanging.
sentences.i: And it was as though they wrecked my shop, smashed my utensils, put me in a chest, and brought the carpenter to make me a gallows-beam, for they meant to hang me.
sentences.n: A stray و stands alone at the end of the previous printed line, before كأنهم; I keep it as the separate word it is printed as. وَجَاوُأ is printed for وَجَاؤُوا, "and they came", with the hamza on the alif; I read jāʾū. جَاءَ بِـ means "bring" (literally "come with"). مَوَاعِين are "utensils, vessels" (singular مَاعُون). The verb يَصْنَعُ follows النَّجَّارِ with no "to": "the carpenter (who) makes". خَشَبَة is a single beam or plank, here the gallows.

sentences.t: فَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَرَى لِي ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ فِى الْمَنَامِ وَلَا كَانَ فِى الْيَقَظَةِ فَضَحِكَتْ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ وَضَمَّتْهُ إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَضَمَّهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī jarā lī dhālika kulluhu fī al-manāmi wa-lā kāna fī al-yaqaẓati fa-ḍaḥikat sittu al-ḥusni wa-ḍammathu ilā ṣadrihā wa-ḍammahā ilā ṣadrihi
sentences.l: So the-praise (is) to-God who it-happened to-me, that all-of-it, in the-sleep, and-not was in the-wakefulness. And-laughed Sitt al-Ḥusn and-pressed-him to her-breast, and-he-pressed-her to his-breast.
sentences.i: "Praise be to God that it all happened to me in a dream, and not in waking life!" Sitt al-Ḥusn laughed and clasped him to her breast, and he clasped her to his.
sentences.n: الَّذِي جَرَى لِي ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ is "who (it) happened to me, all that": the subject ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ comes after the verb. وَلَا كَانَ is "and it was not".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَفَكَّرَ ثُمَّ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَاكَأَنَّهُ إِلَّا فِى الْيَقَظَةِ فَأَنَا مَا عَرَفْتُ أَيْشَ الْقَضِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: thumma tafakkara thumma qāla wa-Allāhi mā-ka-annahu illā fī al-yaqaẓati fa-anā mā ʿaraftu aysha al-qaḍiyyatu
sentences.l: Then he-reflected, then said: By-God, not-as-though-it except in the-wakefulness! So-I not I-knew what (is) the-case.
sentences.i: Then he thought it over and said, "By God, it can only have been in waking life! Yet I do not know what the matter is."
sentences.n: مَاكَأَنَّهُ إِلَّا, "it is as if only", gives "it can only have been". أَيْشَ الْقَضِيَّةُ is "what (is) the case?", with no verb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَامَ وَهُوَ مُتَحَيِّرٌ فِي أَمْرِهِ تَارَةً يَقُولُ أَنَا حَلَمْتُ وَتَارَةً يَقُولُ أَنَا فِى الْيَقَظَةِ وَلَازَالَ كَذَلِكَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu nāma wa-huwa mutaḥayyirun fī amrihi tāratan yaqūlu anā ḥalamtu wa-tāratan yaqūlu anā fī al-yaqaẓati wa-lā-zāla kadhālika ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: Then indeed-he slept, and-he bewildered in his-affair: one-time he-says: I dreamed, and-one-time he-says: I (am) in the-wakefulness; and-not-ceased thus until the-morning.
sentences.i: Then he went to sleep, bewildered about his affair; now he said, "I dreamed," and now, "I am awake"; and so he stayed until morning.
sentences.n: تَارَةً ... وَتَارَةً means "now ... and now". وَلَازَالَ is "and he did not cease", the subject being Badr al-Dīn.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَمُّهُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ الْوَزِيرُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَظَرَ لَهُ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَقَالَ بِاللَّهِ مَا أَنْتَ الَّذِي أَمَرْتَ بِتَكْنِيفِي وَتَسْمِيرِي وَتَخْرِيبِ دُكَّانِي مِنْ شَانِ حَبِّ الرُّمَّانِ لِكَوْنِهِ عَاوِزْ فَافِلْ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalayhi ʿammuhu shamsu al-dīni al-wazīru fa-sallama ʿalayhi fa-naẓara lahu badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-qāla bi-Allāhi mā anta alladhī amarta bi-taknīfī wa-tasmīrī wa-takhrībi dukkānī min shāni ḥabbi al-rummāni li-kawnihi ʿāwiz fāfil
sentences.l: So entered upon-him his-paternal-uncle Shams al-Dīn the-vizier, and-greeted him; and-looked at-him Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and-said: By-God, not you (are) the-one-who ordered my-binding and-my-nailing and-the-wrecking-of my-shop because-of seeds-of the-pomegranate, for-its-being wanting pepper?
sentences.i: Then his uncle Shams al-Dīn the vizier came in to him and greeted him; and Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan looked at him and said, "By God, are you not the one who ordered me bound and nailed up and my shop wrecked, over pomegranate seeds, because it lacked pepper?"
sentences.n: The print has فافل where فُلْفُل, "pepper", is meant, and I point what is printed. تَكْنِيفِي is also doubtful; I take it as "binding me" (perhaps a slip for تَكْتِيفِي, "tying me up"). مَا أَنْتَ الَّذِي, "not you the one who", is a question expecting "yes": "aren't you the one who?". مِنْ شَانِ is colloquial "because of"; عَاوِزْ is Egyptian for "wanting" (Classical يُرِيدُ).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ اعْلَمْ يَا وَلَدِي إِنَّهُ ظَهَرَ الْحَقُّ وَبَانَ مَاهُوَ مُخْتَفِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla lahu al-wazīru iʿlam yā waladī innahu ẓahara al-ḥaqqu wa-bāna mā-huwa mukhtafī
sentences.l: So at that said to-him the-vizier: Know, O my-son, that-it appeared the-truth, and-became-clear what-it hidden.
sentences.i: Then the vizier said to him, "Know, my son, that the truth has come out, and what was hidden has become plain."
sentences.n: إِنَّهُ ظَهَرَ الْحَقُّ has a pronoun "it" that anticipates the subject: "that-it appeared, the truth". مَاهُوَ مُخْتَفِي is "what (it) is hidden"; the print has no tanwīn on the participle.

sentences.t: أَنْتَ ابْنُ أَخِي وَمَا فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى تَحَقَّقْتُ أَنَّكَ الَّذِي دَخَلْتَ عَلَى بِنْتِي ذَاكَ اللَّيْلَةَ وَمَا تَحَقَّقْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا لِكَوْنِكَ عَرَفْتَ الْبَيْتَ وَعَرَفْتَ شَاشَكَ وَسِرْوَا لَكَ وَذَهَبَكَ وَ الْوَرَقَةَ الَّتِي بِخَطِّكَ وَالَّتِي كَتَبَهَا وَالِدُكَ أَخِي
sentences.tr: anta ibnu akhī wa-mā faʿaltu dhālika ḥattā taḥaqqaqtu annaka alladhī dakhalta ʿalā bintī dhāka al-laylata wa-mā taḥaqqaqtu dhālika illā li-kawnika ʿarafta al-bayta wa-ʿarafta shāshaka wa-sirwā laka wa-dhahabaka wa-al-waraqata allatī bi-khaṭṭika wa-allatī katabahā wāliduka akhī
sentences.l: You (are) son-of my-brother. And-not I-did that until I-ascertained that-you (are) the-one-who entered upon my-daughter that the-night; and-not I-ascertained that except because-of-your-being (that) you-knew the-house, and-knew your-turban-cloth and-your-trousers and-your-gold and-the-paper which (is) in-your-handwriting and-which wrote-it your-father, my-brother.
sentences.i: You are my brother's son. I did none of this until I made sure that you were the one who went in to my daughter that night; and I could only be sure because you knew the house, and knew your turban-cloth, your trousers, your gold, and the paper in your handwriting, and the one that your father, my brother, wrote.
sentences.n: A stray و, at the end of a printed line, is kept as its own word before الْوَرَقَةَ.
