The print splits سِرْوَالَكَ into وسروا لك; I point the two printed pieces separately (وَسِرْوَا لَكَ) and the English reads them as "your trousers". ذَاكَ اللَّيْلَةَ uses the masculine "that" with the feminine word for night, and puts it in the accusative as "on that night". عَلَى is the preposition after دَخَلَ for entering upon a bride. وَالِدُكَ أَخِي is "your father, my brother".

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي مَا رَأَيْتُكَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ وَمَاكُنْتُ أَعْرِفُكَ وَإِنَّ أُمَّكَ جِبْتُهَا مَعِي مِنَ الْبَصْرَةِ ثُمَّ رَمَى نَفْسَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَبَكَى
sentences.tr: fa-innī mā raʾaytuka qabla dhālika wa-mā-kuntu aʿrifuka wa-inna ummaka jibtuhā maʿī mina al-baṣrati thumma ramā nafsahu ʿalayhi wa-bakā
sentences.l: For-indeed-I not I-saw-you before that, and-not-I-was I-know-you; and-indeed your-mother, I-brought-her with-me from al-Basra. Then he-threw his-self upon-him and-wept.
sentences.i: For I had never seen you before that, and did not know you; and your mother I brought with me from Basra. Then he threw himself upon him and wept.
sentences.n: جِبْتُهَا is colloquial "I brought her" (Classical جِئْتُ بِهَا). وَمَاكُنْتُ أَعْرِفُكَ is "I did not know you", with كَانَ and a bare imperfect. رَمَى نَفْسَهُ عَلَيْهِ, "threw himself upon him", is the usual way of saying that someone embraced another in a rush of feeling.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ مِنْ عَمِّهِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَعَجَّبَ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَعَانَقَ عَمَّهُ وَبَكَى مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa badru al-dīni ḥasanun min ʿammihi hādhā al-kalāma taʿajjaba ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-ʿānaqa ʿammahu wa-bakā min shiddati al-faraḥi
sentences.l: And-when heard Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan from his-paternal-uncle this the-speech, he-marvelled the-extreme-of the-wonder, and-embraced his-paternal-uncle, and-wept from intensity-of the-joy.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan heard these words from his uncle, he was utterly amazed; he embraced his uncle and wept for sheer joy.
sentences.n: غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ, "the extreme of wonder", is an adverbial accusative: "extremely".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ يَا وَلَدِي إِنَّ سَبَبَ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ مَاجَرَى بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ وَالِدِكَ وَحَكَى لَهُ عَلَى مَاجَرَى بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ أَخِيهِ وَسَبَبِ سَفَرِ وَالِدِهِ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu al-wazīru yā waladī inna sababa dhālika kullihi mā-jarā baynī wa-bayna wālidika wa-ḥakā lahu ʿalā mā-jarā baynahu wa-bayna akhīhi wa-sababi safari wālidihi ilā al-baṣrati
sentences.l: Then said to-him the-vizier: O my-son, indeed the-cause-of that all-of-it (is) what-happened between-me and-between your-father. And-he-related to-him upon what-happened between-him and-between his-brother, and-the-cause-of journey-of his-father to al-Basra.
sentences.i: Then the vizier said to him, "My son, the cause of all that is what passed between me and your father." And he told him what had passed between himself and his brother, and why his father had gone to Basra.
sentences.n: حَكَى لَهُ عَلَى, "he related to him on (the matter of)", is a colloquial "he told him about"; the print joins مَا to جَرَى. The second object, وَسَبَبِ سَفَرِ, "and the cause of the journey", is also governed by عَلَى.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَرْسَلَ خَلْفَ عَجِيبٍ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ وَالِدُهُ قَالَ وَهَذَا الَّذِي ضَرَبَنِي بِالْحَجَرِ فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ هَذَا وَلَدُكَ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ رَمَى نَفْسَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra arsala khalfa ʿajībin fa-lammā raʾāhu wāliduhu qāla wa-hādhā alladhī ḍarabanī bi-al-ḥajari fa-qāla al-wazīru hādhā waladuka fa-ʿinda dhālika ramā nafsahu ʿalayhi wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier sent behind ʿAjīb; and-when saw-him his-father, he-said: And this (is) the-one-who struck-me with-the-stone? And-said the-vizier: This (is) your-son. At that he-threw his-self upon-him and-recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: Then the vizier sent for ʿAjīb; and when the boy's father saw him he said, "And this is the one who struck me with the stone?" The vizier said, "This is your son." Then he threw himself upon him and recited these verses:
sentences.n: أَرْسَلَ خَلْفَ means "sent after", that is, "sent for". عَجِيب, "Wonderful", is a name, here the young son of Badr al-Dīn; وَالِدُهُ, "his father", is Badr al-Dīn himself. The stone is the one that struck his forehead, the "blow" he took for a dream.

sentences.t:
وَلَقَدْ بَكَيْتُ عَلَى تَفَرُّقٍ شَمْلِنَا * قَدْرًا اَفَاضَ الدَّمْعَ مِنْ اَجْفَانِي
وَنَذَرْتُ اِنْ عَادَ الزَّمَانُ يَلُمُّنَا * مَا عُدْتُ اَذْكُرُ فُرْقَةً بِلِسَانِي
هَجَمَ السُّرُورُ عَلَيَّ حَتَّى اَنَّنِي * مِنْ عِظَمِ مَا قَدْ سَرَّنِي اَبْكَانِي
sentences.tr:
wa-laqad bakaytu ʿalā tafarruqi shamlinā * qadran afāḍa al-damʿa min ajfānī
wa-nadhartu in ʿāda al-zamānu yalummunā * mā ʿudtu adhkuru furqatan bi-lisānī
hajama al-surūru ʿalayya ḥattā annanī * min ʿiẓami mā qad sarranī abkānī
sentences.i:
I wept over the scattering of our company, wept until the tears overflowed from my eyelids.
And I vowed that if time should return and gather us, I would never again speak of parting with my tongue.
Joy rushed upon me so that, from the greatness of what gladdened me, it made me weep.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed; note that the print leaves bare alif where Classical writes a hamza (اَفَاضَ, اَجْفَانِي, اَذْكُرُ, اَبْكَانِي). قَدْرًا is adverbial, "to such a degree (that)". In the last line اَنَّنِي "that I" is left without a predicate of its own; the sense runs on into اَبْكَانِي, "it made me weep".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ وَإِذَا بِوَالِدَتِهِ أَقْبَلَتْ وَرَمَتْ نَفْسَهَا عَلَيْهِ وَ أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi wa-idhā bi-wālidatihi aqbalat wa-ramat nafsahā ʿalayhi wa anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And-when he-finished from his-verse, and-behold with-his-mother (she) came-forward, and-threw her-self upon-him, and she-recited, she-says.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses, behold, his mother came in, threw herself upon him, and recited, saying:
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِوَالِدَتِهِ is "and behold, his mother": the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what suddenly appears. The print breaks و from the next word at the line end (و انشدت), and the pointing keeps the break.

sentences.t:
اِذَا الْتَقَيْنَا اِشْتَكَيْنَا * مِنْ عِظَمِ مَا قَدْ نَقُولُ
مَا هُوَ مَلِيحُ الشِّكْوَى * عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ رَسُولْ
sentences.tr:
idhā iltaqaynā ishtakaynā * min ʿiẓami mā qad naqūlu
mā huwa malīḥu al-shikwā * ʿalā lisāni rasūl
sentences.l:
When we-met we-complained * from the-greatness-of what indeed we-say;
not it (is) fair, the-complaint, * upon the-tongue-of a-messenger.
sentences.i: When we meet we complain, so great is what we have to say; complaint is not fair upon a messenger's tongue.
sentences.n: Two couplets, pointed in the print and copied as printed. The point is that a grievance sent by messenger is poor stuff beside saying it face to face, so now that the two have met they complain freely.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ وَالِدَتَهُ حَكَتْ لَهُ عَلَى مَا وَقَعَ لَهَا بَعْدَهُ وَحَكَى لَهَا عَلَى مَا قَاسَاهُ فَشَكَرُوا اللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَلَى اجْتِمَاعِ شَمْلِهِمْ بِبَعْضٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna wālidatahu ḥakat lahu ʿalā mā waqaʿa lahā baʿdahu wa-ḥakā lahā ʿalā mā qāsāhu fa-shakarū Allāha taʿālā ʿalā ijtimāʿi shamlihim bi-baʿḍin
sentences.l: Then indeed his-mother related to-him upon what happened to-her after-him, and-he-related to-her upon what he-suffered; so-they-thanked God, exalted-is-He, upon the-gathering-of their-union with-one-another.
sentences.i: Then his mother told him all that had happened to her after he left, and he told her all that he had suffered; and they thanked God Most High that their company was gathered together again.
sentences.n: حَكَى عَلَى مَا is colloquial: ʿalā marks the matter told, "about what", where Classical would say حَكَى ... مَا. شَمْلُهُمْ is "their union", the same word as in the poem above (شَمْلِنَا), literally "their gathered-togetherness".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ شَمْسَ الدِّينِ ذَهَبَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ بَعْدَ وُصُولِهِ بِيَوْمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra Shams al-Dīn dhahaba ilā al-sulṭāni baʿda wuṣūlihi bi-yawmayni
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier Shams al-Dīn went to the-sultan after his-arrival by two-days.
sentences.i: Then the vizier Shams al-Dīn went to the sultan, two days after his arrival.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَحَيَّاهُ بِتَحِيَّةِ الْمُلُوكِ فَفَرِحَ بِهِ السُّلْطَانُ وَبَشَّ فِي وَحْهِهِ وَأَدْنَاهُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalayhi qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-ḥayyāhu bi-taḥiyyati al-mulūki fa-fariḥa bihi al-sulṭānu wa-bashsha fī waḥhihi wa-adnāhu ilayhi
sentences.l: And-when he-entered upon-him, he-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-greeted-him with-the-greeting-of the-kings; and-rejoiced in-him the-sultan, and-beamed in his-face, and-drew-him-near to-him.
sentences.i: When he came into his presence he kissed the ground before him and greeted him with the salutation due to kings; the sultan was glad of him, beamed upon him, and drew him near.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his two hands", is the usual idiom for "in his presence". The print has وحهه with ح where ج is meant; it is read wajhihi, "his face", and I point the letter as printed. بَشَّ فِي وَجْهِهِ is "he beamed at him" (lit. "in his face").

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اسْتَخْبَرَهُ عَمَّا رَأَى فِي سَفْرَتِهِ وَجَرَى لَهُ فِي ذَهَابِهِ فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِالْقِصَّةِ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا إِلَى آخِرِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma istakhbarahu ʿammā raʾā fī safratihi wa-jarā lahu fī dhahābihi fa-akhbarahu bi-al-qiṣṣati min awwalihā ilā ākhirihā
sentences.l: Then he-asked-him-for-news about-what he-saw in his-journey and-happened to-him in his-going; so-he-informed-him with-the-story from its-first to its-last.
sentences.i: Then he asked him what he had seen on his journey and what had befallen him on the way, and he told him the whole story from beginning to end.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى ظَفَرِكَ بِالْمُرَادِ وَرُجُوعِكَ سَالِمًا إِلَى الْأَهْلِ وَالْأَ وْلَادِ وَلَابُدَّ مِنْ أَنْ أَرَى ابْنَ أَخِيكَ حَسَنَ الْبَصْرِيَّ فَأْتِ بِهِ إِلَى الدِّيوَانِ غَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi ʿalā ẓafarika bi-al-murādi wa-rujūʿika sāliman ilā al-ahli wa-al-awlādi wa-lā budda min an arā ibna akhīka ḥasana al-baṣriyya fa-ʾti bihi ilā al-dīwāni ghadan
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-sultan: The-praise (be) to-God upon your-winning of-the-desired and-your-returning safe to the-family and-the-children; and-no escape from that I-see the-son-of your-brother Ḥasan the-Basran, so-bring with-him to the-court tomorrow.
sentences.i: Then the sultan said to him, "Praise be to God that you won what you sought and have come home safe to your family and children. But I must see your brother's son, Ḥasan al-Baṣrī; bring him to the court tomorrow."
sentences.n: Three printing oddities here. والا ولاد has a stray space inside the word (read wa-al-awlād, "and the children"); I keep the space in the pointing. ولابد is the idiom wa-lā budda min, "and there is no avoiding", printed as one word. فات is فَأْتِ, the imperative "bring" (أَتَى بِـ takes بِـ for the thing brought). Ḥasan al-Baṣrī is Nūr al-Dīn's son; I point the name with iʿrāb like any noun.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ يَحْضُرُ عَبْدُكَ غَدًا إِنْ شَاءَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَخَرَجَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Shams al-Dīn yaḥḍuru ʿabduka ghadan in shāʾa Allāhu taʿālā thumma sallama ʿalayhi wa-kharaja
sentences.l: And-said to-him Shams al-Dīn: Will-attend your-servant tomorrow, if willed God, exalted-is-He. Then he-greeted upon-him and-went-out.
sentences.i: Shams al-Dīn said to him, "Your servant will be present tomorrow, God willing." Then he took his leave and went out.
sentences.n: إِنْ شَاءَاللَّهُ is printed as one word. سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ, "he greeted him", also serves as the farewell when one leaves.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ إِلَى دَارِهِ أَخْبَرَ ابْنَ أَخِيهِ بِاشْتِيَاقِ السُّلْطَانِ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā rajaʿa ilā dārihi akhbara ibna akhīhi bi-ishtiyāqi al-sulṭāni ilayhi
sentences.l: And-when he-returned to his-house he-informed the-son-of his-brother with-the-longing-of the-sultan for-him.
sentences.i: When he got back to his house he told his nephew that the sultan longed to see him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيُّ الْمَمْلُوكُ مُنْقَادٌ لِأَمْرِ مَوْلَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḥasanu al-baṣriyyu al-mamlūku munqādun li-amri mawlāhu
sentences.l: And-said Ḥasan the-Basran: The-owned (is) submissive to-the-command-of his-master.
sentences.i: Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said, "Your servant is obedient to his master's command."
sentences.n: الْمَمْلُوك, "the owned one", is the servant speaking of himself in the third person, a courtly form.

sentences.t: وَالْحَاصِلُ أَنَّهُ ذَهَبَ إِلَى حَضْرَةِ السُّلْطَانِ مَعَ عَمِّهِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ḥāṣilu annahu dhahaba ilā ḥaḍrati al-sulṭāni maʿa ʿammihi Shams al-Dīn
sentences.l: And-the-result (is) that-he went to the-presence-of the-sultan with his-paternal-uncle Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.i: In short, he went to the sultan's presence with his uncle Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.n: وَالْحَاصِلُ, "and the upshot", is the narrator's way of passing over the night in a line.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا حَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ حَيَّاهُ بِأَكْمَلِ التَّحِيَّاتِ وَأَفْضَلِهَا وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِــــعْر
sentences.tr: wa-lammā ḥaḍara bayna yadayhi ḥayyāhu bi-akmali al-taḥiyyāti wa-afḍalihā wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿr
sentences.l: And-when he-attended between his-two-hands, he-greeted-him with-the-most-complete-of the-greetings and-the-best-of-them, and-he-recited, saying: Verse.
sentences.i: And when he stood before him he greeted him with the most perfect and excellent of salutations, and recited, saying:
sentences.n: شعر, "verse", is a heading the print places before a poem (here lengthened with kashīda strokes); it is not spoken, and it will recur before each poem.

sentences.t:
يُقَبِّلُ الْارْضَ مَنْ عَزَّتْ مَرَاتِبُهُ * بِكُمْ وَبِالنُّجْحِ قَدْ فَازَتْ مَطَالِبُهْ
اَنْتُمْ اُولُوا الْمَجْدِ يُحْظَى مَنْ يُؤَمِّلُكُمْ * بِمَا بِهِ فِى اللَّهِ نَا تَعْلُو مَنَا صِبُهْ
sentences.tr:
yuqabbilu al-arḍa man ʿazzat marātibuhu * bikum wa-bi-al-najḥi qad fāzat maṭālibuh
antum ulū al-majdi yuḥẓā man yuʾammilukum * bi-mā bihi fī Allāhi nā taʿlū manā ṣibuh
sentences.l:
Kisses the-ground whoever has-grown-mighty his-ranks * through-you, and-with-the-success indeed have-triumphed his-aims.
You (are) possessors-of the-glory; is-favoured whoever hopes-in-you * with-what by-it, in God nā, rise his-ranks (manā ṣibuh).
sentences.i: He who kisses the ground is one whose ranks have grown mighty through you, and whose aims have triumphed with success. You are the lords of glory; whoever puts his hope in you is granted that by which, through God, his ranks are raised.
sentences.n: Pointed in the print and copied as printed. The second line is partly obscure and perhaps corrupt: فِى اللَّهِ نَا has an unexplained نَا, and مَنَا صِبُهْ is مَنَاصِبُهُ "his ranks" split by a stray space. I read it loosely as "through God, his ranks rise". يُحْظَى is passive, "is made fortunate".

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَ السُّلْطَانُ وَأَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ بِالْجُلُوسِ فَجَلَسَ بِقُرْبِ عَمِّهِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassama al-sulṭānu wa-ashāra ilayhi bi-al-julūsi fa-jalasa bi-qurbi ʿammihi Shams al-Dīn
sentences.l: And-smiled the-sultan and-gestured to-him with-the-sitting, so-he-sat near his-uncle Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.i: The sultan smiled and motioned him to sit, and he sat down beside his uncle Shams al-Dīn.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَأَلَهُ الْمَلِكُ عَنِ اسْمِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَحْقَرُ عَبِيدِكَ الْمَعْرُوفُ بِحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِىِّ الدَّاعِي لَكَ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
sentences.tr: thumma saʾalahu al-maliku ʿan ismihi fa-qāla lahu aḥqaru ʿabīdika al-maʿrūfu bi-ḥasani al-baṣriyyi al-dāʿī laka laylan wa-nahāran
sentences.l: Then asked-him the-king about his-name, and-he-said to-him: The-meanest-of your-servants, the-known by-Ḥasan the-Basran, the-supplicator for-you night and-day.
sentences.i: Then the king asked him his name, and he said, "The humblest of your servants, known as Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who prays for you night and day."
sentences.n: الْبَصْرِىِّ is printed with ى for ي. الْمَعْرُوفُ بِـ is "known as". الدَّاعِي لَكَ, "the one who calls down blessings on you", is a stock phrase of courtly self-description.

sentences.t: فَأَعْجَبَ السُّلْطَانَ كَلَامُهُ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يَمْتَحِنَهُ فِيمَا يَظْهَرُ بِهِ شَأْنُ عِلْمِهِ وَأَدَبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿjaba al-sulṭāna kalāmuhu wa-arāda an yamtaḥinahu fīmā yaẓharu bihi shaʾnu ʿilmihi wa-adabihi
sentences.l: And-pleased the-sultan his-speech, and-he-wanted that he-test-him in-what shows by-it the-matter-of his-knowledge and-his-culture.
sentences.i: His speech pleased the sultan, and he wished to test him in whatever would show the measure of his learning and breeding.
sentences.n: وارادان is printed as one word, wa-arāda an, "and he wished that"; the pointing keeps it joined. أَدَب is the whole polish of a cultured man, manners and letters together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ هَلْ تَحْفَظُ شَيْئًا فِي وَصْفِ الْخَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu hal taḥfaẓu shayʾan fī waṣfi al-khāli
sentences.l: And-said to-him: Do-you-memorise anything in description-of the-mole?
sentences.i: Then he said to him, "Do you know anything by heart in description of the mole?"
sentences.n: الْخَال is the dark mole or beauty-spot on the cheek, a staple of Arabic love poetry. The same word also means "maternal uncle", among many other things, which the sultan is about to ask about.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَأَنْشَدَ شِـــعْــر
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam wa-anshada shiʿr
sentences.l: He-said: Yes. And-he-recited: Verse.
sentences.i: He said, "Yes," and recited:

sentences.t:
حَبِيبٌ كُلَّمَا فَكَّرْتُ فِيهِ * تَوَالَتْ عَبْرَتِي وَعَلَا نَحِيبِي
لَهُ خَالٌ حَكَى حُسْنًا وَلَوْنًا * سَوَادَ الْعَيْنِ اَوْ حَبَّ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr:
ḥabībun kullamā fakkartu fīhi * tawālat ʿabratī wa-ʿalā naḥībī
lahu khālun ḥakā ḥusnan wa-lawnan * sawāda al-ʿayni aw ḥabba al-qulūbi
sentences.l:
A-beloved! Whenever I-thought on-him * followed-one-another my-tears and-rose my-sobbing.
To-him (is) a-mole (that) resembled, in-beauty and-colour, * the-blackness-of the-eye or the-grain-of the-hearts.
sentences.i: A beloved! Whenever I think of him my tears come thick and fast and my sobbing rises. He has a mole that matches, in beauty and in colour, the blackness of the eye or the dark core of hearts.
sentences.n: Pointed in the print and copied as printed. حَبَّ الْقُلُوبِ is the dark inner "grain" of the heart (حَبَّةُ الْقَلْبِ); the print has the plural, "of hearts".

sentences.t: فَاسْتَحْسَنَ الْمَلِكُ الْبَيْتَيْنِ وَقَٰلَ لَهُ هَاتِ غَيْرَهُمَا لِلَّهِ أَبُوكَ وَلَا فُضَّ فُوكَ
sentences.tr: fa-staḥsana al-maliku al-baytayni wa-qāla lahu hāti ghayrahumā li-Allāhi abūka wa-lā fuḍḍa fūka
sentences.l: And-approved the-king the-two-verses and-said to-him: Give other-than-them! To-God (be) your-father, and-not be-broken your-mouth!
sentences.i: The king admired the two verses and said to him, "Give me others! What a father you had, and may your mouth never be broken!"
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال; it is read qāla (dagger alif), a slip that recurs in this night. لِلَّهِ أَبُوكَ, "to God your father", is an exclamation of praise for the father of one who has done well. وَلَا فُضَّ فُوكَ, "may your mouth not be broken", is a blessing; the passive verb is in the perfect, which is how Arabic wishes.

sentences.t: فَأَنْشَدَ شِعْر
sentences.tr: fa-anshada shiʿr
sentences.l: And-he-recited: Verse.
sentences.i: And he recited:

sentences.t:
وَنُقْطَةِ خَالٍ شَبَّهُوهَا بِحَبَّةٍ * مِنَ الْمِسْكِ لَا تَعْجَبْ لِقَوْلِ الَّذِي شَبَّهْ
بَلِ اعْجَبْ لِوَجْهٍ قَدْ حَوَى الْحُسْنَ كُلَّهُ * وَمَا فَاتَهُ مِنْهُ الْجَمِيعُ وَلَا حَبَّهْ
sentences.tr:
wa-nuqṭati khālin shabbahūhā bi-ḥabbatin * mina al-miski lā taʿjab li-qawli alladhī shabbaha
bal iʿjab li-wajhin qad ḥawā al-ḥusna kullahu * wa-mā fātahu minhu al-jamīʿu wa-lā ḥabbah
sentences.l:
And-a-dot-of mole they-likened-it to-a-grain * of the-musk: do-not marvel at-the-saying-of he-who compared.
Rather marvel at-a-face (that) has-contained the-beauty all-of-it, * and-not escaped-it of-it the-whole, nor a-grain.
sentences.i: Many a mole have they likened to a grain of musk; do not marvel at the words of the one who made the comparison. Marvel rather at a face that holds all beauty, so that nothing of it has escaped it, not the whole and not a single grain.
sentences.n: Pointed in the print and copied as printed. The opening وَ is the وَ of رُبَّ, "many a", with the genitive نُقْطَةِ. The conceit is that musk grains are only a small likeness; the real marvel is the face itself. شَبَّهْ and حَبَّهْ end in a pause-form sukun, for the rhyme.

sentences.t: فَاهْتَزَّ الْمَلِكُ طَرَبًا وَقَالَ لَهُ زِدْنِي بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِي عُمْرِكَ فَأَنْشَدَ شِعْر
sentences.tr: fa-ihtazza al-maliku ṭaraban wa-qāla lahu zidnī bāraka Allāhu fī ʿumrika fa-anshada shiʿr
sentences.l: And-was-shaken the-king (with) delight, and-said to-him: Increase-me! God-has-blessed in your-life! And-he-recited: Verse.
sentences.i: The king was stirred with delight and said to him, "Give me more, and may God bless your life!" And he recited:
sentences.n: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ is another perfect-tense wish, "may God bless", like the one in the sentence above.

sentences.t:
يَا مَنْ حَكَى الْخَالَ عَلَى خَدِّهِ * نُقْطَةُ مِسْكٍ فَوْقَ يَا قُوتَهْ
اَنْعِمْ بِوَصْلِي اَلَّا تَكُنْ قَاسِيًا * يَا مُنْيَةَ الْقَلْبِ وَيَا قُوتَهْ
sentences.tr:
yā man ḥakā al-khāla ʿalā khaddihi * nuqṭatu miskin fawqa yāqūtah
anʿim bi-waṣlī allā takun qāsiyan * yā munyata al-qalbi wa-yā qūtah
sentences.l:
O you-who resembled the-mole on his-cheek, * a-dot-of musk above a-ruby;
grant-favour by-my-union that-not you-be cruel, * O wish-of the-heart and-O its-sustenance.
sentences.i: O you whose mole upon your cheek is a dot of musk above a ruby, grant me the favour of union and do not be cruel, O wish of my heart and its sustenance.
sentences.n: Pointed in the print and copied as printed. The grammar of the first line is loose (the verb takes الْخَالَ, yet نُقْطَةُ is nominative), so I take it as "whose mole is a dot of musk". The poet plays on يَا قُوتَهْ, "ruby", printed as two words, and the rhyme-word قُوتَهْ, "its sustenance".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَحْسَنْتَ يَا حَسَنُ وَأَجَدْتَ كُلَّ الْإِ جَادَةِ بَيِّنْ لَنَاكَمْ لِلَفْظِ الْخَالِ مِنْ مَعْنًى فِىاللُّغَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku aḥsanta yā ḥasanu wa-ajadta kulla al-ijādati bayyin lanā-kam li-lafẓi al-khāli min maʿnan fī al-lughati
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-king: You-did-well, O Ḥasan, and-you-excelled all the-excelling! Make-clear to-us how-many, for-the-word-of the-mole, of meaning in-the-language.
sentences.i: Then the king said to him, "Well done, Ḥasan, and you have excelled in every way! Tell us how many meanings the word khāl has in the language."
sentences.n: الا جادة is printed with a stray space for الإجادة; كُلَّ الْإِجَادَةِ is "all the excelling", i.e. "in every way". لناكم is لَنَا كَمْ, "to us how many", printed as one word. فىاللغة is فِي اللُّغَةِ run together, with ى for ي; this running-together of فى and the article recurs and will not be noted again.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَيَّدَ اللَّهُ الْمَلِكَ ثَمَانِيَةٌ وَخَمْسُونَ مَعْنًى وَقِيلَ خَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ayyada Allāhu al-malika thamāniyatun wa-khamsūna maʿnan wa-qīla khamsūna
sentences.l: And-said to-him: God-has-supported the-king: eight-and-fifty (in) meaning, and-it-was-said fifty.
sentences.i: He said to him, "May God support the king: fifty-eight meanings, and some say fifty."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ صَدَقْتَ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ أَلَكَ عِلْمٌ بِتَفْصِيلِ الْحُسْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ṣadaqta thumma qāla lahu a-laka ʿilmun bi-tafṣīli al-ḥusni
sentences.l: And-said to-him: You-spoke-truly. Then he-said to-him: Is-there-to-you knowledge of-the-detailing-of the-beauty?
sentences.i: He said to him, "You have spoken truly." Then he asked him, "Do you know the particulars of beauty?"
sentences.n: أَلَكَ عِلْمٌ is "do you have knowledge": the question-hamza أَ, then لَكَ "to you".

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ الصَّبَاحَةُ فِىالْوَجْهِ الْوَضَاءَةُ فِىالْبَشَرَةِ الْجَمَالُ فِىالْأَنْفِ الْحَلَاوَةُ فِىالْعَيْنَيْنِ الْمَلَاحَةُ فِىالْفَمِ الظَّرْفُ فِىاللِّسَانِ الرَّشَاقَةُ فِىالْقَدِّ اللَّبَاقَةُ فِىالشَّمَائِلِ كَمَالُ الْحُسْنِ فِىالشَّعْرِ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam al-ṣabāḥatu fī al-wajhi al-waḍāʾatu fī al-basharati al-jamālu fī al-anfi al-ḥalāwatu fī al-ʿaynayni al-malāḥatu fī al-fami al-ẓarfu fī al-lisāni al-rashāqatu fī al-qaddi al-labāqatu fī al-shamāʾili kamālu al-ḥusni fī al-shiʿri
sentences.l: He-said: Yes. The-radiance in the-face; the-lustre in the-skin; the-beauty in the-nose; the-sweetness in the-two-eyes; the-charm in the-mouth; the-elegance in the-tongue; the-slenderness in the-stature; the-grace in the-dispositions; the-perfection-of the-beauty in the-hair.
sentences.i: He said, "Yes: radiance belongs to the face, lustre to the skin, beauty to the nose, sweetness to the eyes, charm to the mouth, elegance to the tongue, slenderness to the stature, grace to the manners, and the perfection of beauty to the hair."
sentences.n: Each word names a quality proper to one feature, and English can only approximate them: ṣabāḥa is a bright, fair face, waḍāʾa a clear shining skin, malāḥa a piquant charm, ẓarf refined wit, rashāqa slim lightness, labāqa tactful grace. شَمَائِل is "dispositions, ways" (in verse, the traits of character). The poem that follows gives the same list in verse.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ جَمَعَ هَذَا كُلَّهُ الشِّهَابُ الْحِجَازِيُّ فِي أَبْيَاتٍ مِنْ بَحْرِ الرَّجَزِ وَهِيَ هَذِهِ شِعْر
sentences.tr: wa-qad jamaʿa hādhā kullahu al-shihābu al-ḥijāziyyu fī abyātin min baḥri al-rajazi wa-hiya hādhihi shiʿr
sentences.l: And-indeed gathered this all-of-it al-Shihāb the-Hijazi in verses from the-sea-of the-rajaz, and-they (are) these: Verse.
sentences.i: And all this was gathered together by al-Shihāb al-Ḥijāzī in verses in the rajaz metre, which are these:
sentences.n: الشِّهَابُ الْحِجَازِيُّ is the poet the text names. بَحْر, "sea", is the technical word for a verse metre; رَجَز is the simple, quick metre in which didactic verse is often written.

sentences.t:
صَبَاحَةُ الْوَجْهِ قُلْ وَالْبَشَرَةْ لَهَا * وَضَاءَةٌ فَكُنْ ذَا تَبْصِرَهْ
وَبِالْجَمَالِ الْاَنْفُ حَقًّا يُوصَفُ * وَبِالْحَلَاوَةِ الْعُيُونُ تُعْرَفُ
نَعَمْ وَقَالُوا لِلْفَمِ الْمَلَاحَهْ * فَافْهَمْهُ عَنِّي لَاعَدِمْتَ الرَّاحَهْ
وَالظَّرْفُ فِى اللِّسَانِ وَالرَّشَاقَهْ * لِلْمَقَلِ وَالشَّمَائِلُ اللَّبَاقَهْ
ثُمَّ كَمَالُ الْحُسْنِ قَالُوا فِى الشِّعْرِ * فَاصْغِ اِلَى نَظْمِي وَكُنْ مِمَّنْ عَذَرْ
sentences.tr:
ṣabāḥatu al-wajhi qul wa-al-basharah * lahā waḍāʾatun fa-kun dhā tabṣirah
wa-bi-al-jamāli al-anfu ḥaqqan yūṣafu * wa-bi-al-ḥalāwati al-ʿuyūnu tuʿrafu
naʿam wa-qālū li-al-fami al-malāḥah * fa-afhamhu ʿannī lā-ʿadimta al-rāḥah
wa-al-ẓarfu fī al-lisāni wa-al-rashāqah * li-al-maqali wa-al-shamāʾilu al-labāqah
thumma kamālu al-ḥusni qālū fī al-shiʿri * fa-iṣghi ilā naẓmī wa-kun mimman ʿadhar
sentences.l:
Radiance-of the-face, say, and-the-skin * for-it (is) lustre, so-be possessor-of insight.
And-with-beauty the-nose truly is-described * and-with-sweetness the-eyes are-known.
Yes, and-they-said for-the-mouth the-charm, * so-understand-it from-me; may-you-not-lack the-ease.
And-the-elegance (is) in the-tongue, and-the-slenderness * for the-eyeballs, and-the-dispositions the-grace.
Then the-perfection-of the-beauty, they-said, (is) in the-hair; * so-incline to my-verse and-be of whoever excused.
sentences.i: Say that radiance belongs to the face, and lustre to the skin, and be a person of insight. The nose is rightly described by beauty, and the eyes are known by sweetness. Yes, and they said that charm belongs to the mouth; take this from me, and may you never lack ease. Elegance is in the tongue, slenderness is for the eyes, and the manners have grace. Then, they said, the perfection of beauty is in the hair; so listen to my verse, and be one who forgives.
sentences.n: Pointed in the print and copied as printed (the double space after لَهَا in the first line is a hemistich break). The poem repeats the prose list, with one difference: here رَشَاقَة goes with the eyes (لِلْمَقَلِ, "for the eyeballs"), where the prose gave it to the stature. I keep what is printed. In the last line the print points الشِّعْرِ with a kasra, shiʿr, "poetry", where the sense is shaʿr, "hair"; I keep the printed pointing and translate "hair", though the poet may be punning on his own verse. Several lines end in a sukun for the pause (تَبْصِرَهْ, الْمَلَاحَهْ, الرَّاحَهْ, عَذَرْ).

sentences.t: فَسُرَّ السُّلْطَانُ بِكَلَامِهِ وَاسْتَأْنَسَ بِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ مَا مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِمْ فِى الْمَثَلِ شُرَيْحٌ أَدْهَى مِنَ الثَّعْلَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-surra al-sulṭānu bi-kalāmihi wa-istaʾnasa bihi thumma qāla lahu mā maʿnā qawlihim fī al-mathali Shurayḥun adhā mina al-thaʿlabi
sentences.l: And-was-pleased the-sultan with-his-speech and-took-comfort in-him; then he-said to-him: What (is) the-meaning-of their-saying in the-proverb: Shurayḥ (is) more-cunning than the-fox?
sentences.i: The sultan was delighted with his talk and took pleasure in his company; then he said to him, "What is the meaning of the saying in the proverb, 'Shurayḥ is craftier than the fox'?"
sentences.n: فسر is read as the passive فَسُرَّ, "was pleased"; the print has no marks to tell it from فَسَّرَ, "explained", but the sense decides. شريح is Shurayḥ, the judge of early Islamic Kūfa, proverbial for shrewdness; the answer is the little story that follows. Note too that فى is printed with ى for في; I point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَيَّدَكَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَنَّ شُرَيْحًا خَرَجَ أَيَّامَ الطَّاعُونِ إِلَى النَّجَفِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku ayyadaka Allāhu taʿālā anna Shurayḥan kharaja ayyāma al-ṭāʿūni ilā al-najafi
sentences.l: And-he-said: Know, O king — has-supported-you God the-Exalted — that Shurayḥ went-out (in) the-days-of the-plague to al-Najaf,
sentences.i: He said: "Know, O king, may God Most High strengthen you, that Shurayḥ went out during the days of the plague to Najaf,
sentences.n: أَيَّدَكَ اللَّهُ is a wish phrased as a past verb, "may God support you", a courtly formula you will meet constantly. النجف is al-Najaf in Iraq, the high ground beside Kūfa.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ إِذَا قَامَ يُصَلِّى يَجِيئُ ثَعْلَبٌ فَيَقِفُ تُجَاهَهُ وَيُحَاكِيهِ فَيَشْغَلُهُ عَنْ صَلَوتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna idhā qāma yuṣallī yajīʾu thaʿlabun fa-yaqifu tujāhahu wa-yuḥākīhi fa-yashghaluhu ʿan ṣalawtihi
sentences.l: And-he-was, when he-stood (to) pray, (there) comes a-fox, and-stands facing-him, and-imitates-him, and-so-occupies-him from his-prayer.
sentences.i: It was his habit that whenever he stood to pray, a fox would come and stand facing him and mimic him, and so distract him from his prayer.
sentences.n: A past كان with a bare imperfect in the clauses that follow expresses habit, "it used to happen that". يصلى is printed with ى for يصلي; there is no mark to add.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَالَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ نَزَعَ يَوْمًا قَمِيصَهُ فَجَعَلَهُ عَلَى قَصَبَةٍ وَأَخْرَجَ كُمَّيْهِ وَجَعَلَ عِمَامَتَهُ عَلَيْهَا وَشَدَّ وَسَطَهَا وَنَصَبَهَا فِي مَحَلِّ صَلَوتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭāla dhālika ʿalayhi nazaʿa yawman qamīṣahu fa-jaʿalahu ʿalā qaṣabatin wa-akhraja kummayhi wa-jaʿala ʿimāmatahu ʿalayhā wa-shadda wasaṭahā wa-naṣabahā fī maḥalli ṣalawtihi
sentences.l: And-when grew-long that upon-him, he-took-off one-day his-shirt, and-put-it on a-reed, and-put-out its-two-sleeves, and-put his-turban upon-it, and-bound its-middle, and-set-it-up in the-place-of his-prayer.
sentences.i: When this had gone on too long for him, one day he took off his shirt and hung it on a reed, with the sleeves held out, set his turban on top of it, bound its middle, and stood it up in the place where he prayed.
sentences.n: The sleeves held out and the belted middle make a scarecrow in the shape of a man at prayer. فلما طال ذلك عليه, "when that grew long upon him", is an idiom for "when it wore on him".

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ الثَّعْلَبُ عَلَى عَادَتِهِ فَوَقَفَ بِإِزَائِهِ وَأَتَاهُ شُرَيْحٌ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ فَأَخَذَهُ فَقِيلَ مَا قِيلَ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala al-thaʿlabu ʿalā ʿādatihi fa-waqafa bi-izāʾihi wa-atāhu Shurayḥun min khalfihi fa-akhadhahu fa-qīla mā qīla
sentences.l: And-came-on the-fox upon its-custom, and-stood opposite-it; and-came-to-it Shurayḥ from behind-it and-seized-it; and-was-said what was-said.
sentences.i: The fox came on as was its habit and stood facing it, and Shurayḥ came up on it from behind and seized it; and so the saying was made."
sentences.n: فَقِيلَ مَا قِيلَ, "and what was said was said", is a way of cutting the story short: the proverb about Shurayh and the fox is what came of it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ السُّلْطَانُ مَا كَشَفَ عَنْهُ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيِّ قَالَ لِعَمِّهِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ إِنَّ ابْنَ أَخِيكَ هَذَا كَامِلٌ فِي فَنِّ الْأَدَبِ وَلَا أَظُنُّ أَنَّ مِثْلَهُ يُوجَدُ فِي مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-sulṭānu mā kashafa ʿanhu Ḥasanu al-Baṣriyyi qāla li-ʿammihi Shamsi al-Dīni inna ibna akhīka hādhā kāmilun fī fanni al-adabi wa-lā aẓunnu anna mithlahu yūjadu fī Miṣra
sentences.l: And-when heard the-sultan what he-uncovered of-it Ḥasan the-Basran, he-said to-his-uncle Shams al-Dīn: Indeed the-son-of your-brother this (is) perfect in the-art-of the-letters, and-not I-think that his-like is-found in Egypt.
sentences.i: When the sultan had heard what Ḥasan al-Baṣrī revealed of himself, he said to Ḥasan's uncle Shams al-Dīn, "This nephew of yours is accomplished in the art of letters, and I do not think his like is to be found in Egypt."
sentences.n: الأدب, adab, is polite learning: poetry, anecdote, eloquence and courtly manners together. مصر is Miṣr, Egypt (the tale is set in Cairo).

sentences.t: فَقَامَ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيِّ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَعَدَ قُعُودَ الْمَمْلُوكِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ مَوْلَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma Ḥasanu al-Baṣriyyi wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qaʿada quʿūda al-mamlūki bayna yaday mawlāhu
sentences.l: And-stood Ḥasan the-Basran and-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-sat the-sitting-of the-slave between the-two-hands-of his-master.
sentences.i: Ḥasan al-Baṣrī rose and kissed the ground before him, and sat down as a slave sits before his master.
sentences.n: بين يديه, "between his two hands", means "in front of him, in his presence". Kissing the ground is the courtier's act of homage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ لَمَّا اطَّلَعَ عَلَى حَقِيقَةِ مَاتَحَصَّلَ لِحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ مِنَ الْعُلُومِ الْأَ دَبِيَّةِ فَرِحَ فَرَحًا عَظِيمًا وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً فَاخِرَةً وَقَلَّدَهُ أَمْرًا يَسْتَعِينُ بِهِ عَلَى مَا يُصْلِحُ حَالَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-sulṭāna lammā iṭṭalaʿa ʿalā ḥaqīqati mātaḥaṣṣala li-Ḥasani al-Baṣriyyi mina al-ʿulūmi al-a dabiyyati fariḥa faraḥan ʿaẓīman wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿatan fākhiratan wa-qalladahu amran yastaʿīnu bihi ʿalā mā yuṣliḥu ḥālahu
sentences.l: Then indeed the-sultan, when he-became-aware-of the-truth-of what-had-accrued to-Ḥasan the-Basran from the-sciences the-literary, rejoiced a-rejoicing great; and-bestowed upon-him a-robe-of-honour, splendid, and-invested-him (with) an-order by-which he-might-help-himself towards what would-set-right his-state.
sentences.i: Then, when the sultan learned the truth of what Ḥasan al-Baṣrī had mastered of the literary arts, he rejoiced greatly, and bestowed on him a splendid robe of honour, and invested him with a decree by which he might set his circumstances right.
sentences.n: The print divides الأدبية after the article, الأ دبية; I point the two pieces as printed. ماتحصل is printed as one word, "what had accrued". خلعة is the robe of honour a ruler gives to mark favour. أمرا is an order or decree; the text does not say whether it granted a post or a stipend.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيِّ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَدَعَالَهُ بِالْعِزِّ الدَّائِمِ وَاسْتَأْذَنَهُ لِلذَّهَابِ مَعَ عَمِّهِ الْوَزِيرِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ فَأَذِنَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāma Ḥasanu al-Baṣriyyi wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-daʿālahu bi-al-ʿizzi al-dāʾimi wa-istaʾdhanahu li-al-dhahābi maʿa ʿammihi al-wazīri Shamsi al-Dīni fa-adhina lahu
sentences.l: Then stood Ḥasan the-Basran and-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-prayed-for-him with-the-glory the-everlasting, and-asked-his-leave for-the-going with his-uncle the-vizier Shams al-Dīn; and-he-permitted to-him.
sentences.i: Then Ḥasan al-Baṣrī rose, kissed the ground before him, and prayed that he might have lasting glory; and he asked leave to go with his uncle the vizier Shams al-Dīn, and the sultan gave him leave.
sentences.n: ودعاله is printed as one word, دَعَا لَهُ, "he prayed for him", the usual courtly blessing at a leave-taking.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ وَأَتَى هُوَ وَعَمُّهُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فَقَدَّمَ لَهُمَا الطَّعَامَ فَأَكَلَا مَا يَسَّرَاللَّهُ لَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja wa-atā huwa wa-ʿammuhu ilā al-bayti fa-qaddama lahumā al-ṭaʿāma fa-akalā mā yassaraAllāhu lahumā
sentences.l: And-he-went-out, and-came he and-his-uncle to the-house; and-presented to-them-both (someone) the-food, and-they-two-ate what made-easy God for-them-both.
sentences.i: He went out, and he and his uncle came to the house, where the food was set before them, and they ate what God had provided for them.
sentences.n: Nobody is named as the one who served the food; فقدم is simply "one presented", and English says it with a passive. يسراللَّه is printed as one word, يَسَّرَ اللَّهُ, "God made easy", i.e. provided.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيِّ بَعْدَ الْفَرَاغِ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ مَجْلِسَ امْرَأَتِهِ سِتِّ الْحُسْنِ وَأَخْبَرَهَا بِمَا اتَّفَقَ لَهُ فِي حَضْرَةِ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala Ḥasanu al-Baṣriyyi baʿda al-farāghi mina al-ṭaʿāmi majlisa imraʾatihi Sitti al-Ḥusni wa-akhbarahā bi-mā ittafaqa lahu fī ḥaḍrati al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: Then entered Ḥasan the-Basran, after the-finishing from the-food, the-sitting-room-of his-wife Sitt al-Ḥusn, and-informed-her of-what befell to-him in the-presence-of the-sultan.
sentences.i: Then, when the meal was over, Ḥasan al-Baṣrī went into the room of his wife, Sitt al-Ḥusn, and told her what had befallen him in the sultan's presence.
sentences.n: ست الحسن, Sitt al-Ḥusn, means "Lady of Beauty" (ست is the Egyptian form of سَيِّدَة, "lady"). مجلس is the sitting-room, here the lady's own apartment. أخبرها بما اتفق له: أَخْبَرَ takes بِـ for the news told.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ أَنْ يَجْعَلَكَ نَدِيمًا لَهُ وَيُوَفِّرَ لَكَ الصِّلَاتِ وَالْهِبَاتِ وَأَنْتَ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ كَالنَّهْرِ الْأَ عْظَمِ تَسْطَعُ أَنْوَارُكَمَا لِكَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ فِي بَرًّا وَبَحْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu lā budda min an yajʿalaka nadīman lahu wa-yuwaffira laka al-ṣilāti wa-al-hibāti wa-anta bi-faḍli Allāhi ka-al-nahri al-a ʿẓami tasṭaʿu anwārukamā lika ḥaythumā kunta fī barran wa-baḥrin
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: There-is-no-avoiding that he-make-you a-boon-companion to-him and-multiply for-you the-gifts and-the-bounties. And-you, by-the-grace-of God, (are) like-the-river the-greatest: shine the-lights-of-your-perfection wherever you-are, in land and-sea.
sentences.i: She said to him, "He is bound to make you his boon companion and to heap gifts and bounties on you. And you, by God's grace, are like the mightiest of rivers: the lights of your perfection shine wherever you are, on land and sea."
sentences.n: نديم is the cup-companion, the ruler's intimate at table. The print writes انواركما لك; I read أنوار كمالك, "the lights of your perfection", and point the two pieces to match (أَنْوَارُكَمَا + لِكَ). A dual "your two lights" would not agree with the single "you". The print also divides الأ عْظَمِ and ends with برا, which I point as printed (barran) and read as "on land".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أُرِيدُأَنْ أَقُولَ تَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِهِ لِتَزْدَادَ مَحَبَّتِي فِي قَلْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā urīduʾan aqūla taṣīdatan fī madḥihi li-tazdāda maḥabbatī fī qalbihi
sentences.l: So-he-said to-her: I-want-that I-say a-poem in his-praise, so-that-increase my-love in his-heart.
sentences.i: He said to her, "I want to compose an ode in his praise, so that the love of me in his heart may grow."
sentences.n: اريدان is printed as one word, أُرِيدُ أَنْ, "I want to"; I point it as printed. تصيدة has ت where قصيدة (qaṣīda, an ode) has ق; I point the letter printed and read it qaṣīda. لِتَزْدَادَ is لِـ of purpose, "so that", with the subjunctive.

sentences.t: قَاتْ لَهُ أَصَبْتَ فِيمَا نَوَيْتَ فَجَوِّدِ الْفِكْرَةَ وَتَأَنَّقْ فِيمَا تَقُولُ وَمَا أَرَاهُ إِلَّا مُقَابِلًا لَكَ بِالْقَبُولِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu aṣabta fīmā nawayta fa-jawwidi al-fikrata wa-taʾannaq fīmā taqūlu wa-mā arāhu illā muqāblan laka bi-al-qabūli
sentences.l: She-said to-him: You-were-right in-what you-intended; so-make-good the-thought and-take-pains in-what you-say; and-not I-see-him except meeting you with-acceptance.
sentences.i: She said to him, "You are right in what you intend. So perfect your thought, and take pains over what you say; I expect nothing but that he will receive you with favour."
sentences.n: قات is printed for قالت, the ل dropped; read qālat, "she said". Pointing can only mark what is printed, so the word is pointed as printed. وما أراه إلا مقابلا لك بالقبول is a litotes: "I see him as nothing but one who meets you with acceptance", i.e. he is sure to accept it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْفَرَدَ حَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيِّ نَاحِيَةً وَنَمَّقَ أَبْيَاتًا رَشِيقَةَ الْمَبَانِي حَسَنَةَ الْمَعَانِي وَهِيَ هَذِهِ —
sentences.tr: thumma infarada Ḥasanu al-Baṣriyyi nāḥiyatan wa-nammaqa abyātan rashīqata al-mabānī ḥasanata al-maʿānī wa-hiya hādhihi —
sentences.l: Then withdrew Ḥasan the-Basran (to) a-side, and-embellished verses, graceful-of the-structures, fair-of the-meanings; and-they (are) these:
sentences.i: Then Ḥasan al-Baṣrī withdrew to one side and polished some verses, graceful in build and fair in meaning, and they were these:
sentences.n: المباني / المعاني, "structures / meanings", rhyme: the print's own jingle (sajʿ), kept in the English only as a balance. The dash at the end is printed in the edition and marks the coming poem.

sentences.t:
لِيْ هُمَامٌ قَدْسَمَا اَوْجَ الْعُلَى * وَهْوَ فِيْ نَهْجِ الْكِرَامِ الْغُرِّ سَالِكْ
اَمَّرَ الاَقْطَارَ طُرًّا عَدْلُهُ * وَعَلَى اَعْدَائِهِ سَلَّ الْمَسَالِكْ
ضَيْغَمٌ شَهْمٌ تَقِيٌّ اِنْ تَقُلْ * مَلِكٌ اَوْ مَلَكٌ فَهْوَ كَذلِكْ
يَرْجِعُ الْعَافِي غَنِيًّا اِنْ تَرُمْ * وَصْفَهُ تَعْجِزُ عَنْهُ فِيْ مَقَالِكْ
هُوَ صُبْحٌ مُسْفِرٌ يَوْمَ الْعَطَا * وَهْوَ فِيْ يَوْمِ الْوَغَى كَاللَّيْلِ حَالِكْ
قَلَّدَ الاَعْنَاقَ مِنَّا جُودُهُ * وَهْوَ بِالاِحْسَانِ لِلاَحْرَارِ مَالِكْ
طَوَّلَ اللهُ لَنَا فِيْ عُمْرِهِ * وَوَقَاهُ شَرَّ اَحْدَاثِ الْمَهَالِكْ
sentences.tr:
lī humāmun qadsamā awja al-ʿulā * wa-huwa fī nahji al-kirāmi al-ghurri sālik
ammara al-aqṭāra ṭurran ʿadluhu * wa-ʿalā aʿdāʾihi salla al-masālik
ḍayghamun shahmun taqiyyun in taqul * malikun aw malakun fa-huwa kadhālik
yarjiʿu al-ʿāfī ghaniyyan in tarum * waṣfahu taʿjizu ʿanhu fī maqālik
huwa ṣubḥun musfirun yawma al-ʿaṭā * wa-huwa fī yawmi al-waghā ka-al-layli ḥālik
qallada al-aʿnāqa minnā jūduhu * wa-huwa bi-al-iḥsāni li-al-aḥrāri mālik
ṭawwala Allāhu lanā fī ʿumrihi * wa-waqāhu sharra aḥdāthi al-mahālik
sentences.l:
To-me (is) a-great-one, has-risen (to) the-zenith-of the-heights, * and-he on the-path-of the-noble the-radiant (is) a-traveller.
Has-set-in-command the-regions altogether his-justice, * and-against his-enemies he-has-drawn the-roads.
A-lion, spirited, godfearing; if you-say * a-king or an-angel, then-he (is) like-that.
Returns the-suppliant rich; if you-seek * his-description, you-are-unable of-it in your-speech.
He (is) a-dawn shining on-the-day-of the-giving, * and-he on the-day-of the-battle like-the-night (is) pitch-black.
Has-collared the-necks from-us his-generosity, * and-he by-the-beneficence of-the-free (is) master.
Has-lengthened God for-us in his-life, * and-has-shielded-him (from) the-evil-of the-mishaps-of the-perils.
sentences.i: I have a noble lord who has climbed to the summit of eminence, and who walks the path of the generous and the radiant. His justice has ruled all the regions, and against his enemies he has cut off the roads. He is a bold lion, godfearing: call him king or call him angel, and he is just that. The suppliant goes home rich; if you try to describe him, you are lost for words. He is a shining dawn on the day of giving, and on the day of battle he is dark as night. His generosity has hung a collar on our necks, and by kindness he is master of the free. May God lengthen his life for us and shield him from the evil of perils and mishaps.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied exactly as printed. The poem rhymes throughout in -ālik, with the final sukūn the print marks. قَدْسَمَا is one word in the print, qad samā, "has risen". In line 2 اَمَّرَ is obscure: as pointed it is ammara, "set in command, made an emirate of", and it may be a misprint for ʿammara, "made flourish"; the second half, سَلَّ الْمَسَالِكْ, "drew the roads", is also unclear, and I take it as "cut off the ways (of his enemies)" in the sense of closing them. The word الْعَافِي, in line 4, is the one who comes seeking favour. In line 5 الْعَطَا is for الْعَطَاءِ with the hamza dropped, a licence of verse. وَهْوَ is read wa-huwa; the sukūn on the ه is the metre's way of spelling it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ تَحْرِيرِهَا أَرْسَلَ بِهَا إِلَى حَضْرَةِ السُّلْطَانِ صُحْبَةَ عَبْدٍ مِنْ عَبِيدِ عَمِّهِ الْوَزِيرِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min taḥrīrihā arsala bihā ilā ḥaḍrati al-sulṭāni ṣuḥbata ʿabdin min ʿabīdi ʿammihi al-wazīri Shamsi al-Dīni
sentences.l: And-when he-finished from its-writing, he-sent with-it to the-presence-of the-sultan, in-company-of a-slave from the-slaves-of his-paternal-uncle the-vizier Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.i: When he had finished writing it out, he sent it to the presence of the sultan by the hand of one of the slaves of his uncle, the vizier Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.n: The subject, never named here, is Ḥasan, who has just finished the verses. حَضْرَةُ السُّلْطَانِ, "the presence of the sultan", is the courtly way of saying "the sultan himself". The prefix بِـ in أَرْسَلَ بِهَا is the one the verb chooses: "send with it" means "send it".

sentences.t: فَاطَّلَعَ عَلَيْهَا الْمَلِكُ وَسُرَّ خَاطِرُهُ بِهَا وَقَرَاَهَا لِلْحَاضِرِينَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَأَثْنَوْا عَلَيْهِ ثَنَاءً عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-iṭṭalaʿa ʿalayhā al-maliku wa-surra khāṭiruhu bihā wa-qaraʾahā li-al-ḥāḍirīna bayna yadayhi fa-athnaw ʿalayhi thanāʾan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: And-he-looked-over upon-it the-king, and-was-gladdened his-mind with-it, and-he-read-it to-the-present-ones between his-hands, and-they-praised upon-him a-praise great.
sentences.i: The king looked it over and was delighted with it, and he read it aloud to those present before him, and they praised Ḥasan highly.
sentences.n: اطَّلَعَ عَلَى is "look into, become acquainted with". بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his hands", means "in front of him, in his presence"; you will meet it again in this passage. خَاطِر is the mind or heart, the seat of one's feelings.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اسْتَدْعَاهُ إِلَى مَجْلِسِهِ فَحَضَرَ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَنْتَ مِنْ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ نَدِيمِي وَقَدْ عَيَّنْتُ لَكَ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ مَعَ مَا قَلَّدْتُكَ بِهِ سَابِقًا
sentences.tr: thumma istadʿāhu ilā majlisihi fa-ḥaḍara fa-qāla lahu al-maliku anta min hādhā al-yawmi nadīmī wa-qad ʿayyantu laka fī kulli shahrin alfa dirhamin maʿa mā qalladtuka bihi sābiqan
sentences.l: Then he-summoned-him to his-assembly, and-he-came; and-said to-him the-king: You, from this the-day, (are) my-boon-companion; and-indeed I-have-appointed for-you in every month a-thousand dirhams, with that-which I-invested-you with-it formerly.
sentences.i: Then he summoned him to his court, and he came. The king said to him, "From this day you are my boon companion, and I have appointed for you a thousand dirhams every month, besides what I bestowed on you before."
sentences.n: نَدِيم is the boon companion, the one who sits drinking and talking with a ruler, from the verb نَادَمَ that appears later in this night. قَلَّدَهُ بِـ is "to invest him with (an office or gift)": the بِـ in بِهِ points back to مَا, "that with which I invested you".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ حَسَنٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَدَعَا لَهُ بِدَوَامِ الْعِزِّ وَطُولِ الْبَقَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma Ḥasanun al-Baṣriyyu wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi thalātha marrātin wa-daʿā lahu bi-dawāmi al-ʿizzi wa-ṭūli al-baqāʾi
sentences.l: And-rose Ḥasan the-Basran, and-kissed the-ground between his-hands three times, and-prayed for-him with-the-continuance-of the-glory and-the-length-of the-remaining.
sentences.i: Ḥasan of Basra rose and kissed the ground before him three times, and prayed for him, that his glory might endure and his life be long.
sentences.n: ثلث is printed for ثلاث, "three", and is pointed with a dagger alif (thalātha); the same short spelling is common in this print. دَعَا لَهُ بِـ is "to pray for him for (something)": the بِـ introduces what is prayed for, "continuance of glory".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ حَسَنً الْبَصْرِيَّ عَلَا قَدْرُهُ وَطَارَ صِيتُهُ فِى الْبُلْدَانِ وَبَقِيَ فِي أَجْمَلِ حَالٍ وَأَرْغَدِ عَيْشٍ مَعَ عَمِّهِ وَأَهْلِهِ إِلَى أَنْ أَدْرَكَتْهُ الْوَفَاةُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Ḥasanan al-Baṣriyya ʿalā qadruhu wa-ṭāra ṣītuhu fī al-buldāni wa-baqiya fī ajmali ḥālin wa-arghadi ʿayshin maʿa ʿammihi wa-ahlihi ilā an adrakathu al-wafātu
sentences.l: Then indeed Ḥasan the-Basran: rose his-rank, and-flew his-renown in the-lands, and-he-remained in the-most-beautiful-of state and-the-most-abundant-of life with his-paternal-uncle and-his-family, until reached-him the-death.
sentences.i: After that, Ḥasan of Basra rose in rank, and his fame flew through the lands, and he lived on in the finest state and the easiest of lives with his uncle and his family, until death overtook him.
sentences.n: After إِنَّ the name is put in the accusative, and then a whole clause (عَلَا قَدْرُهُ, "his rank rose") says what he did: this is the usual way to resume a story after a pause. أَجْمَلِ حَالٍ and أَرْغَدِ عَيْشٍ are superlatives followed by an indefinite noun, "the most beautiful of states", "the most abundant of lives".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْقِصَّةَ هَٰرُونُ الرَّشِيدُ مِنْ لِسَانِ جَعْفَرٍ تَعَجَّبَ وَقَٰلَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُكْتَبَ هَذِهِ الْأَحَادِيثُ بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-qiṣṣata Hārūnu al-Rashīdu min lisāni Jaʿfarin taʿajjaba wa-qāla yanbaghī an tuktaba hādhihi al-aḥādīthu bi-māʾi al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And-when he-heard the-story Hārūn al-Rashīd from the-tongue-of Jaʿfar, he-marvelled, and-he-said: It-is-fitting that be-written these the-tales with-water-of the-gold.
sentences.i: When Hārūn al-Rashīd heard the story from the lips of Jaʿfar, he marvelled and said, "These tales ought to be written in letters of gold."
sentences.n: Two spellings to know. هرون is printed without the alif for ā (Hārūn), so it is pointed with a dagger alif; and قل is printed for قال, pointed qāla in the same way. بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ, "with water of gold", is the phrase for writing in gold ink, a mark of the highest honour for a text.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَطْلَقَ الْعَبْدَ وَأَمَرَبِأَنْ يُعَيَّنَ لِلشَّابِّ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مَا يَطِيبُ بِهِ عَيْشُهُ وَوَهَبَ سُرِّيَّةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَصَارَ مِمَّنْ يُنَادِمُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma aṭlaqa al-ʿabda wa-amara bi-an yuʿayyana li-al-shābbi fī kulli shahrin mā yaṭību bihi ʿayshuhu wa-wahaba surriyyatan min ʿindihi wa-ṣāra mimman yunādimuhu
sentences.l: Then he-released the-slave, and-commanded that be-allotted to-the-youth in every month that-which is-pleasant with-it his-living; and-he-gave a-concubine from at-him; and-he-became from-those-whom he-keeps-company-with.
sentences.i: Then he let the slave go, and ordered that the youth be allotted each month whatever would make his life pleasant. He gave him a concubine from his own household, and the youth became one of his boon companions.
sentences.n: The print runs وأمر and بأن together as وامربان; I point it as one word (wa-amara bi-an) and keep it unspaced. أَمَرَ بِـ "command (that)" takes بِـ with أَنْ and a passive verb here: "that it be allotted". سُرِّيَّة is a slave-girl kept as a concubine. The subject changes in the last clause: it is the youth who becomes one of Hārūn's companions (ممن ينادمه, "of those who keep him company").

sentences.t: وَمَا هَذَا بِأَ عْجَبَ مِنْ حِكَايَةِ الْخَيَّاطِ وَالْأَحْدَبِ وَالْيَهُودِيِّ وَالشَّاهِدِوَا لنَّصْرَانِيِّ وَمَا وَقَعَ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-mā hādhā bi-aʿjaba min ḥikāyati al-khayyāṭi wa-al-aḥdabi wa-al-yahūdiyyi wa-al-shāhidi wa-al-naṣrāniyyi wa-mā waqaʿa lahum
sentences.l: And-not this (is) more-wondrous than the-tale-of the-tailor and-the-hunchback and-the-Jew and-the-witness and-the-Christian, and-what befell them.
sentences.i: And this is no more wonderful than the tale of the tailor, the hunchback, the Jew, the witness and the Christian, and what happened to them.
sentences.n: Three oddities of print. بأ عجب is spaced as two words (با عجب) and I read it as the one word بِأَعْجَبَ, "more wondrous"; the pointing keeps the gap and puts a sukūn on the ع. The spacing at والشاهدوا لنصراني is also off: the sense is والشاهد والنصراني, with the و ا ل of the last word split across the space, so I point the first word with an extra وَا and the second with the bare ل of an elided article. مَا هَذَا بِأَعْجَبَ is the usual way to say "this is no more wonderful than...", with بِـ after a negative nominal sentence. الشاهد is "the witness" (it can also be a legal officer who attests); the print does not say which here, so I give the plain sense.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَكَيْفَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla al-maliku wa-kayfa kāna dhālika
sentences.l: Said the-king: And-how was that?
sentences.i: The king said, "And how was that?"

sentences.t: قَٰلَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي قَدِيمِ الزَّمَانِ وَسَالِفِ الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَوَانِ فِي مَدِينَةِ الصِّينِ رَجُلٌ خَيَّاطٌ مَبْسُوطُ الْأَنَامِلِ يُحِبُّ اللَّهْوَ وَالطَّرَبَ وَكَانَ يَخْرُجُ هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَحْيَانِ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ عَلَى التَّفَرُّجَاتِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu kāna fī qadīmi al-zamāni wa-sālifi al-ʿaṣri wa-al-awāni fī madīnati al-Ṣīni rajulun khayyāṭun mabsūṭu al-anāmili yuḥibbu al-lahwa wa-al-ṭaraba wa-kāna yakhruju huwa wa-zawjatuhu fī baʿḍi al-aḥyāni yatafarrajūna ʿalā al-tafarrujāti
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O king the-fortunate, that-he there-was in the-ancient-time-of the-time and-the-bygone-age-of the-age and-the-era, in the-city-of China, a-man, a-tailor, outstretched-of the-fingertips, he-loves the-diversion and-the-merriment; and-he-used-to-go-out, he and-his-wife, in some-of the-times, they-amusing-themselves upon the-amusements.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that in the ancient days and bygone ages and times, in the city of China, there lived a tailor, open-handed, who loved diversion and merrymaking. He and his wife used to go out now and then to take their pleasure in the sights.
sentences.n: قلت is printed for قالت; it is read qālat, "she said" (Shahrazād). The opening formula is in rhymed prose (sajʿ): الزَّمَانِ / الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَوَانِ. مَبْسُوطُ الْأَنَامِلِ is literally "spread of fingertips", a figure for a free-handed, generous man; the sense is a little uncertain, since it could also mean "well-off". The plural verb يَتَفَرَّجُونَ after هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ is a loose agreement in the print; it describes the pair. التَّفَرُّجَات is "the amusements, the sights".

sentences.t: فَخَرَجُوا يَوْمًا مِنْ أَوَّلِ النَّهَارِ وَرَجَعُوا آخِرَهُ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسَاءِ فَوَجَدُوا فِي طَرِيقِهِمْ رَجُلًا أَحْدَبَ رُؤْيَتُهُ تُضْحِكُ الْمَغْبُونَ وَتُزِيلُ الْهَمَّ عَنِ الْمَحْزُونِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajū yawman min awwali al-nahāri wa-rajaʿū ākhirahu ilā manzilihim ʿinda al-masāʾi fa-wajadū fī ṭarīqihim rajulan aḥdaba ruʾyatuhu tuḍḥiku al-maghbūna wa-tuzīlu al-hamma ʿani al-maḥzūni
sentences.l: And-they-went-out one-day from the-first-of the-daytime, and-returned its-last to their-home at the-evening; and-they-found in their-road a-man, hunchbacked, his-sight makes-laugh the-cheated and-removes the-worry from the-grieved.
sentences.i: One day they went out at the start of the day and came back at its end, toward evening, and on their way they came upon a hunchbacked man whose very sight would make the downcast laugh and lift the care from the grieving.
sentences.n: The edition prints آخره and رؤيته with the hamza already written, so those are kept as printed. الْمَغْبُون is one who has been cheated or wronged, and so one who is low in spirits. رَجُلًا أَحْدَبَ, "a hunchbacked man", is the Hunchback who gives the tale its name. The two halves of the description are balanced for the ear, تُضْحِكُ الْمَغْبُونَ / تُزِيلُ الْهَمَّ عَنِ الْمَحْزُونِ, again in rhymed prose.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ الْخَيَّاطُ وَزَوْجَتُهُ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ عَزَمُوا عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُوحَ مَعَهُمْ إِلَى بَيْتِهِمْ لِيُنَادِمَهُمْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ فَأَجَابَهُمْ وَمَشَى مَعَهُمْ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-khayyāṭu wa-zawjatuhu yatafarrajūna ʿalayhi thumma innahum ʿazamū ʿalayhi an yarūḥa maʿahum ilā baytihim li-yunādimahum tilka al-laylata fa-ajābahum wa-mashā maʿahum ilā al-bayti
sentences.l: And-at that advanced the-tailor and-his-wife, they-amusing-themselves upon-him; then indeed-they they-urged upon-him that he-go with-them to their-house, so-that-he-keep-them-company that the-night; and-he-answered-them, and-walked with-them to the-house.
sentences.i: At that the tailor and his wife went up to him and watched him with amusement, and then they pressed him to go along with them to their house and keep them company that night. He agreed, and walked with them to the house.
sentences.n: عَزَمَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ is "to press him to, to invite him urgently"; عَلَى is the preposition this verb takes for the person pressed. لِيُنَادِمَهُمْ is لِـ with a subjunctive, "so that he might keep them company": it states the purpose of the invitation. يَرُوحُ is "go", a colloquial favourite in the Nights.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الْخَيَّاطُ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَكَانَ اللَّيْلُ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ فَاشْتَرَى سَمَكًا مَقْلِيًّا وَخُبْزًا وَلِيمُونًا وَعَقِيدًا يَحْلُو بِهِ وَأَتَى وَحَطَّ السَّمَكَ قُدَّامَ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-khayyāṭu ilā al-sūqi wa-kāna al-laylu qad aqbala fa-ishtarā samakan maqliyyan wa-khubzan wa-līmūnan wa-ʿaqīdan yaḥlū bihi wa-atā wa-ḥaṭṭa al-samaka quddāma al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-went-out the-tailor to the-market, and-the-night had indeed drawn-near; and-he-bought fish fried, and-bread, and-lemon, and-thickened-syrup, it-turns-sweet with-it; and-he-came, and-set-down the-fish in-front-of the-hunchback.
sentences.i: The tailor went out to the market, for night had already fallen, and bought fried fish and bread and lemons and a sweet syrup to sweeten the meal with. Then he came back and set the fish down in front of the hunchback.
sentences.n: عَقِيد is a thickened sweet syrup (what is boiled down until it sets); يَحْلُو بِهِ is compressed, "it turns sweet with it", and I take it as the syrup that sweetens the meal. قُدَّامَ is the everyday word for "in front of" (Classical would be أَمَامَ).

sentences.t: وَأَكَلُوا فَأَخَذَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ جَزْلَةَ سَمَكٍ كَبِيرَةً وَلَقَّمَتْهَا لِلْأَحْدَبِ وَسَدَّتْ فَمَهُ بِكَفِّهَا
sentences.tr: wa-akalū fa-akhadhati imraʾatu al-khayyāṭi jazlata samakin kabīratan wa-laqqamathā li-al-aḥdabi wa-saddat famahu bi-kaffihā
sentences.l: And-they-ate; and-took the-woman-of the-tailor a-big-piece-of fish, large, and-fed-it (as a morsel) to-the-hunchback, and-stopped his-mouth with-her-palm.
sentences.i: They began to eat, and the tailor's wife took a large chunk of fish and crammed it into the hunchback's mouth, and shut his mouth with her hand.
sentences.n: جَزْلَة is a thick piece or chunk. لَقَّمَهُ is "to feed someone a morsel", and the person fed takes لِـ here (لِلْأَحْدَبِ, "to the hunchback"). The edition prints امرأة with the hamza already on the alif, and so that is kept as printed. سَدَّ فَمَهُ بِكَفِّهَا is "she stopped his mouth with her palm": بِـ is the instrument.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا تَأْكُلُهَا إِلَّا دَفْعَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي فَرْدِ نَفَسٍ وَلَا أُمْهِلُكَ حَتَّى تَمْضَغَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wa-Allāhi mā taʾkuluhā illā dafʿatan wāḥidatan fī fardi nafasin wa-lā umhiluka ḥattā tamḍaghahā
sentences.l: And-she-said: By-God, not you-eat-it except one-gulp, one, in a-single-of breath; and-not I-give-you-respite until you-chew-it.
sentences.i: And she said, "By God, you will eat it in one go, in a single breath, and I will not give you time to chew it!"
sentences.n: وَاللَّهِ is the oath: وَ here means "by" and takes the genitive. مَا تَأْكُلُهَا إِلَّا دَفْعَةً is "you will not eat it except in one go", a forceful way of saying "you shall swallow it whole" (the imperfect carries the sense of a command). The edition prints تأكلها with the hamza already on the alif, so that is kept as printed. فِي فَرْدِ نَفَسٍ is "in a single breath", literally "in one of breath".

sentences.t: فَبَلَعَهَا وَكَانَتْ فِيهَا شَوْكَةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ فَانْشَبَكَتْ فِي حَلْقِهِ مَعَ انْقِضَاءِ أَجَلِهِ فَمَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-balaʿahā wa-kānat fīhā shawkatun qawiyyatun fa-inshabakat fī ḥalqihi maʿa inqiḍāʾi ajalihi fa-māta
sentences.l: And-he-swallowed-it; and-there-was in-it a-thorn, strong; and-it-became-entangled in his-throat, with the-ending-of his-appointed-term; and-he-died.
sentences.i: He swallowed it, and in it was a strong bone, which stuck in his throat just as his appointed time ran out, and he died.
sentences.n: شَوْكَة is literally "a thorn", here a fish-bone. انْشَبَكَ is the form meaning "to become entangled, stuck". أَجَل is a person's appointed term of life, the moment fixed for his death; مَعَ انْقِضَاءِ أَجَلِهِ, "with the ending of his term", says that the bone struck just when his hour came. Death arrives with fierce speed in the Nights, and the tale's trouble begins here.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-reached Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the closing formula that ends each night, in rhymed prose (الصَّبَاحُ / الْمُبَاحِ). الْكَلَام الْمُبَاح is "the permitted speech", the storytelling that she is allowed to do until daybreak. Shahrazād is in the accusative as the object of أَدْرَكَ, and the diptote ending shows it as -a.
